4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: From us / in our presence / with us — denoting nearness, possession, or origin from a particular side. 'ʿInd' marks something held at, coming from, or belonging to a party.
5.grammar: An adverb of place ('at the presence of') with the attached pronoun '-nā' ('us/our'). It is a frozen form fixed in the genitive, the '-i' state being the form such a word takes; the whole means 'with us' or 'from our side'.
5.root: عِنۡد (ʿind) — a frozen adverb of place ('at, near, in the presence of'); not derived from a verbal root

6.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

7.meaning: Kill! / Fight! — a command addressed to a group to slay or put to death. The bare, forceful core meaning of taking life, directed at more than one person.
7.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group of males/mixed, 'kill!' The ending -ū is the plural 'you-all' command marker: it directs the order at several people rather than one. The initial vowelled 'u-' is a helping prefix that lets the otherwise vowel-less command be pronounced.
7.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, slay, put to death; to fight

8.meaning: 'Sons / children' — the plural of 'son,' the male offspring; by extension descendants. It is the broken plural of ibn.
8.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun. The final -a marks it as a direct object (the thing the verb acts upon) or otherwise in the accusative state. The plain -a (not -an) here goes with the word being definite or bound to a following word in a possessive ('of') link. The pattern abnāʾ is the plural of ibn.
8.root: ب-ن-ي / ب-ن-و (b-n-w/y) — son, child; to build

9.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
9.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
10.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

11.meaning: Together with him; in his company or alongside him.
11.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment, 'with', joined to the attached pronoun -hu 'him'. Together they mean 'with him / in his company'.

12.meaning: A command meaning 'and let (the females) live / spare them, keep them alive' — to leave alive rather than kill. The verb-form means to cause or allow something to remain living; it is also tied to 'shame/modesty' from the same root, but in this shape it is the keeping-alive sense.
12.grammar: A plural command (imperative) addressed to 'you (men): let live / spare!' The is-ta- prefix forms a derived stem of the verb, and the -ū ending directs the order to a male plural audience. The starting 'i-' (hamzat al-waṣl) is a helping vowel that drops in connected speech.
12.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — to live, be alive; (related sense) modesty, shame

13.meaning: 'Their women / their womenfolk'; the plural noun for women, with the possessive 'their'.
13.grammar: A plural noun. The -a ending is the accusative case, marking it as the object of a verb. The attached -hum means 'their' (referring to a male-inclusive group), so the whole is 'their women'.
13.root: ن-س-و (n-s-w) — woman, womankind

14.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
14.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
14.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

15.meaning: A scheme / a plot / a cunning stratagem — a carefully devised plan, often with a connotation of guile or trickery aimed at another.
15.grammar: A noun. The -u ending is the nominative case, typically marking it as the subject or the thing being spoken about. It is also commonly the first term of an 'of' phrase (e.g., 'the scheme of …').
15.root: ك-ي-د (k-y-d) — to plot, scheme, contrive a stratagem

16.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
16.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
16.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

17.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
17.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

18.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
18.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

19.meaning: Means 'straying / error / being lost' — wandering off the right path, the opposite of guidance, whether literally losing one's way or going astray in belief and conduct.
19.grammar: An abstract noun: 'straying / error.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite) — the case a noun takes after a preposition or in a possessive link, e.g. 'in an error.' The long -ā- belongs to this noun-pattern.
19.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: Pharaoh; the title/name of the ruler of ancient Egypt, used as a proper name.
2.grammar: A proper noun (a foreign name, which does not take nunation). The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence (the one doing the action).

3.meaning: A command meaning 'leave me / let me be / allow me' with 'me' attached — an order to step aside and let the speaker proceed with what he intends.
3.grammar: A plural command ('you all, leave!') with the object 'me' attached. The -ū marks the order to a plural audience. Before the 'me' pronoun comes a buffering nūn (nūn al-wiqāya) that protects the verb's ending, then the yāʾ is 'me' as the receiver of the action. The verb dhar- is used only in present/command forms.
3.root: و-ذ-ر (w-dh-r) — to leave, let alone, forsake

4.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning '(that) I kill / I slay,' first-person singular. As a bare action-word it denotes the speaker putting someone to death.
4.grammar: Present-tense verb, first-person singular: 'I kill.' The a- prefix means 'I.' The final consonant carries no vowel (jussive/'cut-off' state, shown by the sukūn), the form that follows words of intention or condition ('so that I may…' / 'if…') and signals an outcome dependent on something else.

5.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
5.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)
5.root: — (proper name; non-Arabic origin)

6.meaning: A command-by-implication meaning 'and let him call / pray / invoke' — directing that a third party should summon or call upon someone. The root spans calling out, summoning, and supplicating.
6.grammar: A third-person command formed with the 'lām of command': 'let him call.' The ya- marks 'he,' and the l- prefix turns the statement into an order aimed at someone absent. The final weak letter (wāw) is dropped to a bare -u in this jussive/command state, since the root ends in a weak letter.
6.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, supplicate

7.meaning: The noun 'Lord' joined to a 'his' pronoun — 'his Lord'. Rabb conveys the Master and Sustainer who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; far richer than 'lord' alone.
7.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'). The -a ending is accusative, the case used when the noun is an object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case; -hu means it belongs to 'him'.
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

8.meaning: 'Indeed I / truly I' — an emphasis particle ('verily, indeed') that strongly affirms a statement, fused with the attached pronoun 'I.'
8.grammar: The particle inna asserts and emphasizes the statement that follows ('indeed, truly, it is certainly the case that…'). It governs its noun in the accusative; that governed noun (the ism of inna) is the attached pronoun -ī, 'I/me,' which functions as the subject of the inna-clause. The predicate then follows. So inna here takes 'I' as its accusative-governed subject.
8.root: — (particle + pronoun, no triliteral root)

9.meaning: I fear, I am afraid of, I stand in awe/dread — expressing the speaker's own fear, whether dread of harm or reverent awe.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks the doer as 'I'. The final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual state ('I fear / I am fearing').

10.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
10.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

11.meaning: A verb meaning '(that) he change / alter / replace / substitute' — to swap one thing for another or transform a state into a different one. The doubled-letter form stresses a thorough, deliberate changing.
11.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular, on the doubled-middle-letter (intensive) pattern: 'he changes/replaces.' The final -a is the subjunctive ending, the state a verb takes after words meaning 'that / so that / lest' — pointing to a possible or intended outcome rather than a present fact.
11.root: ب-د-ل (b-d-l) — to change, exchange, replace, substitute

12.meaning: Your religion / way of life — the system of belief, worship, obedience, and accountability one lives by; 'dīn' carries the sense of a binding way to which one submits and for which one is recompensed.
12.grammar: A singular noun carrying the accusative '-a' ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb. The attached '-kum' is a possessive pronoun meaning 'your' for a plural addressee ('you all').
12.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, way; obedience, requital, accountability

13.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
13.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

14.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
14.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
14.root: — (particle; no root)

15.meaning: A verb meaning '(that) he make appear / bring to light / cause to spread / make manifest' — to bring something into the open or make it prevail. The causative form means to make something become outwardly visible.
15.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular, in the causative (make-something-happen) stem: 'he makes appear.' The final -a is the subjunctive ending, used after 'that / so that / lest' to express a purpose or intended result rather than a simple statement of fact.
15.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — to appear, become visible; back, to prevail

16.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
16.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

17.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
17.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

18.meaning: Corruption, ruin, disorder, mischief — the state of things being spoiled or broken, the opposite of soundness and good order.

parts.en: corruption / ruin (the final -a is the accusative case ending, marking the direct object)

18.grammar: A definite noun (with 'al-' = 'the') meaning 'corruption.' The final -a on 'fasāda' is the accusative case ending, which commonly marks the noun as a direct object ('… loves not corruption') or otherwise as something acted upon.
18.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — corruption, spoilage, disorder, the opposite of rightness

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: Mūsā (Moses), the prophet — a proper name.
2.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. It is indeclinable — its ending (the long final 'ā') does not change to show case — so the same form serves whether it functions as subject, object, or after a preposition.

3.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
3.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

4.meaning: 'I have sought / taken refuge' — to seek protection and shelter in someone, fleeing to them for safety from a threat.
4.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb with the ending -tu, which means 'I' did the action and that it is already done: 'I sought refuge.' The -tu is the first-person singular past ending.
4.root: ع-و-ذ (ʿ-w-dh) — to seek refuge, take shelter, protect oneself

5.meaning: With/in my Lord; the preposition 'with/by/in' joined to 'Lord' (Rabb — the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and nurtures) and the pronoun 'my'.
5.grammar: The prefixed 'bi' is a preposition ('with, in, by'), which forces the following noun into the genitive ('-i'). 'Rabb' denotes one who owns, sustains and nurtures. The attached '-ī' means 'my'. Used here for Allah, the term is rendered 'Lord'.
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master

6.meaning: 'And your Lord' — Rabb means the Lord, Master, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, owns, governs, and provides for all. The ending adds 'your (plural),' and 'wa-' means 'and.'
6.grammar: A noun, 'Lord/Sustainer,' with the possessive ending '-kum' ('your,' for a group). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case-vowel, the form a noun takes when possessed by ('…of you') or after a preposition/oath particle. Prefixed 'wa-' here can mean 'and' or introduce an oath ('by').
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; Lord, Sustainer

7.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
7.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

8.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
8.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.
8.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, comprising the whole

9.meaning: 'An arrogant one / a haughty person' — one who magnifies himself, swelling with self-importance and looking down on others. The form names someone who actively makes himself out to be greater than he is.
9.grammar: An active participle of the 'self-magnifying' stem ('one who makes himself great'). The -in ending marks it as indefinite ('an arrogant one') and in the genitive state — typically following a preposition or linked to a preceding noun. The mu- prefix identifies the doer of the action.
9.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great; (this stem) to be arrogant, haughty

10.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
10.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

11.meaning: He believes; he has faith. The verb denotes giving heartfelt trust and assent, especially affirming faith in Allah and what He has revealed; the form also carries the sense of granting security.
11.grammar: A present/future verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he' for this verb pattern (form IV), and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain ongoing or habitual statement.

12.meaning: 'On the Day of …' — the word 'day' with the preposition 'in/on' attached, used to fix the time of an event. By itself 'day' is a span of time; with 'on' it points to when something occurs.

parts.en: day (with genitive -i required after the preposition)

12.grammar: The noun 'day' preceded by the preposition bi- ('in/on'). The -i ending is genitive, which is required after a preposition and also links the word to a following noun ('the Day OF …'). So the form expects another noun after it to complete the phrase.
12.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, time, period

13.meaning: The reckoning, accounting, or calling to account — the tallying and settling of deeds; also calculation or counting in a general sense.
13.grammar: A definite verbal noun with the article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i (kasra) marks the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or as the second part of a possessive pair ('… of the reckoning').
13.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to count, calculate, reckon

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: A man; an adult male human being.
2.grammar: A singular noun marked indefinite ('a man'). The final -un (tanwīn) combines the -u nominative case-ending — typically marking the doer or subject of a sentence — with the -n that signals indefiniteness ('a man' rather than 'the man').

3.meaning: 'Believing / faithful (man)' — a masculine adjective/participle for one who has faith in Allah.

parts.en: believing, faithful (masculine active participle) + indefinite nominative '-un'

3.grammar: A masculine singular active participle ('a believing man'). The mu- prefix forms the doer of a form-IV verb (one who believes). The final -un (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and nominative — the case for a subject or a description matching an indefinite nominative noun.
3.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust; form IV: to believe, have faith

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: The family, folk, or close people of someone — those belonging to a person's household, following, or kin.
5.grammar: A singular collective noun in the genitive (-i ending), which typically links it to a following noun ('the folk OF …') or follows a preposition. It points to those associated with a named person.
5.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, kinsfolk (āl is derived from ahl by elision of the hāʾ)

6.meaning: Pharaoh — the title/name of the ruler of ancient Egypt, used as a proper name for that figure.
6.grammar: A proper name. Being a foreign, non-inflecting (diptote) name, it takes a single -a for both the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn. Here it follows another noun in a possessive link ('… of Pharaoh').

7.meaning: He/it conceals, keeps hidden, suppresses, or holds back from disclosure — to deliberately keep something secret rather than make it known.
7.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he' or 'it'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, the plain present-tense form used to state that the action happens or is ongoing ('he conceals / is concealing').

8.meaning: His faith — the inner belief, trust, and assent of the heart, here possessed by a single male individual. 'Īmān' is the act of believing and entrusting oneself, especially the deep conviction that secures the heart.
8.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -hu ending means 'his / of him' (third-person masculine singular owner). The -a vowel before it is the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
8.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust, faith

9.meaning: Will you (all) kill / slay? — an indignant question put to a group, challenging them over the act of killing a person.
9.grammar: A present/imperfect verb opened by the interrogative prefix a- ('do…?, will…?'). The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The -ūna ending is also the indicative mood, the plain present-tense form used for an action that is happening or will happen.

10.meaning: 'A man' — an adult male human being. The word denotes a man specifically as a male individual, often with a sense of full-grown manhood.
10.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks the indefinite accusative, typically the case of a direct object or of a predicate following certain particles.
10.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — manhood, the adult male; (also the foot/to go on foot)

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
11.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

12.meaning: To say, utter, or speak — to give voice to words.
12.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a masculine singular doer, 'he'. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which the verb takes after certain particles (such as 'so that', 'until', or 'in order to'), giving a sense of a dependent or intended action.
12.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

13.meaning: My Lord, Master, and Sustainer — the One who owns, nurtures, and governs me; expressing ownership together with intimate care.
13.grammar: A masculine noun with the attached first-person possessive ("my"). The suffix -iya means "my" and, being a possessive ending, fixes the noun's relationship rather than leaving it to a case vowel. It denotes that the Lord is being claimed as one's own.
13.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
14.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
14.root: — (proper divine name)

15.meaning: 'And indeed / while already' — the word 'wa' ('and, while') joined to 'qad', a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
15.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and', or circumstantial 'while') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' emphasizes completion and certainty ('has indeed already…'); with a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes' or 'may'.

16.meaning: "he/it came to you" — a past verb "came" with the pronoun "you" as the one reached, i.e. something arrived at or reached a group of people.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base third-person masculine singular form ("he/it came"), with no extra subject suffix. The verb "to come" is intransitive, so the attached -kum is not a direct object but an indirect (dative) pronoun — "to you" (masculine plural), equivalent to "came to you (all)."

17.meaning: 'With the clear proofs / evident signs' — bayyināt are plain, self-evident demonstrations that make the truth manifest, leaving no doubt.
17.grammar: Built from 'bi-' ('with/by means of') + 'al-' ('the') + a feminine plural noun meaning 'clear proofs.' The -i ending is the genitive case, required after the preposition 'bi-'; the feminine sound plural '-āt' takes -i (not -a) in this case. The whole phrase means 'with the clear proofs.'

18.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
18.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

19.meaning: 'Your Lord' (addressing a group). 'Rabb' is a rich term: the Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, possesses, provides for, and brings a thing to its proper completion — far more than a mere ruler.
19.grammar: A noun ('Lord') with an attached possessive pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. 'Rabb' carries a doubled (geminated) 'b' — the shaddah — at its core. The '-i' vowel on 'rabb' is its case ending, determined by 'Lord's' own role in the sentence (not by the suffix); the attached '-kum' is the possessor ('your'), addressing a plural 'you', and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive.

20.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
20.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

21.meaning: A shortened form of the verb 'to be' meaning 'he/it is' or 'he/it was' — the core verb expressing existence or the state of being something.
21.grammar: An imperfect verb 'to be', third-person masculine singular, in the clipped (jussive) mood used after negation or conditions. From a weak root, its final consonant is normally yakun; here that last letter is dropped for lightness, leaving yaku ('he/it is/was').
21.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to pass

22.meaning: A liar — one who speaks falsehood, who says what is untrue. As an active participle it describes a person characterized by lying.
22.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word on the fāʿil pattern, فَاعِل, meaning 'one who does X') used as a noun or description: 'a lying one, a liar'. The final -an is the indefinite accusative ending: it marks an indefinite noun ('a …') that is functioning as an object or as a predicate/description.

23.meaning: 'Then upon Him / so on Him' — the preposition 'upon/on' with the pronoun 'him', preceded by 'then/so', conveying that something rests upon or is directed onto him.
23.grammar: A connective 'fa-' ('then / so', often showing result) with the preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon'), whose form shifts to 'ʿalay-' when a pronoun is attached. The pronoun takes the -hi form (rather than -hu) because it follows the 'ay' sound. Placing this phrase first typically gives a sense of 'upon Him [alone] …'.

24.meaning: His lie / his falsehood — an untrue statement attributed to a single male speaker; the act or content of his lying.
24.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -hu ending means 'his / of him' (third-person masculine singular owner). The -u vowel before it is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or stands as the main thing being spoken about.

25.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
25.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

26.meaning: A shortened form of the verb 'to be' meaning 'he/it is' or 'he/it was' — the core verb expressing existence or the state of being something.
26.grammar: An imperfect verb 'to be', third-person masculine singular, in the clipped (jussive) mood used after negation or conditions. From a weak root, its final consonant is normally yakun; here that last letter is dropped for lightness, leaving yaku ('he/it is/was').
26.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to pass

27.meaning: Truthful, honest — one who tells the truth and whose word matches reality. As an active participle it describes a person characterized by truthfulness.

parts.en: truthful one / one who tells the truth

27.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word on the fāʿil pattern, فَاعِل, meaning 'one who does X') used as a description: 'a truthful one'. The final -an is the indefinite accusative ending: it marks an indefinite noun ('a …') functioning as an object or as a predicate/description.

28.meaning: It will strike you / befall you / afflict you — used of a calamity, harm, or affliction reaching and hitting a group of people.
28.grammar: A present/imperfect Form IV (afʿala) verb meaning 'to strike / befall / afflict'. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The attached -kum means 'you all' as the object (the ones struck). The stem ends in a vowelless (jussive) form, the shortened mood used after conditional or negative particles meaning 'would/should/let it…'.
28.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — hitting the mark, striking, befalling

29.meaning: Some, a part, a portion — a piece or subset of a larger whole. As a noun it points to 'some of' a group or thing rather than all of it.
29.grammar: A singular noun meaning 'a part / some.' The final -u marks the nominative case, used for the subject of a sentence; it is commonly followed by a noun in the 'of' (genitive) form to mean 'some of …'.

30.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
30.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

31.meaning: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'he promises you' or 'he holds out (something) to you' — to pledge or hold out a prospect of something to a plural 'you'. Neutral in itself, it can introduce a good promise or a threat.
31.grammar: Present/future verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The -u on the stem is the indicative ending, the default mood for an ongoing or factual statement. The attached -kum is the direct-object pronoun 'you (plural)'.

32.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
32.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

33.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
33.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

34.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
34.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

35.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
35.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
35.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

36.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
36.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

37.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
37.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

38.meaning: One who is excessive, extravagant, or wasteful — a person who oversteps proper limits, squandering or going to harmful extremes. Often used of transgressing the bounds Allah has set.

parts.en: one who is excessive / a transgressor of limits

38.grammar: An active participle of the Form IV (afʿala) pattern, naming the doer: 'one who commits excess'. The final -un is the indefinite nominative ending: it marks an indefinite noun ('a …') that serves as the subject of a sentence or as the main predicate describing the subject.
38.root: س-ر-ف (s-r-f) — exceeding the proper limit, excess, waste

39.meaning: 'A persistent liar / great liar' — an intensive form denoting someone who lies habitually and abundantly, not merely once. The pattern stresses the depth and frequency of the falsehood.
39.grammar: An intensive noun-of-character on the faʿʿāl pattern (doubled middle letter = doing something a great deal). The -un ending marks it as indefinite ('a great liar') and in the subject/doer (nominative) state. The doubled 'dh' (-dhdh-) conveys the intensification.

1.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
1.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
1.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

2.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something is done or given.
2.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). Such prepositions assign a benefit, purpose, or recipient. The pronoun's vowel appears as '-u' (kumu) to ease pronunciation when a word follows.

3.meaning: 'The kingship / sovereignty / dominion' — al-mulk is rule and royal authority itself, the power and right to govern.
3.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence (the thing that 'is' or does something).
3.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — ownership, dominion, kingship

4.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'the day,' very often used to mean 'today' or 'this day.' With the definite article it points to the present day as a defined, known span of time, and by extension can denote 'now' or 'the present moment.'
4.grammar: A masculine noun carrying the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' is the accusative ending; on a noun of time it commonly marks it as an adverb answering 'when?' — fixing the action to that period ('on the day', 'today').
4.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

5.meaning: Dominant / prevailing / uppermost — those who are on top, who have the upper hand, who prevail over others. The word describes being manifest, evident, and victorious over an opponent.
5.grammar: An active participle (Form I, fāʿil pattern) in the masculine sound plural, accusative or genitive case, marked by -īna. As an active participle it describes 'those who are prevailing / dominating'. The -īna ending marks either accusative or genitive for the sound masculine plural — the two cases share the same ending.
5.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — back, surface, outward appearance; to be manifest, prevail, be on top

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

7.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
7.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

8.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
8.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

9.meaning: He/it helps us, aids us, gives us victory — to come to the support of a group and defend or rescue them, especially against an enemy.
9.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The attached -nā means 'us' as the object (the ones helped). The -u before the suffix is the indicative mood, the plain present-tense form for an action that happens or is ongoing ('he helps').

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: Might, force, or severe punishment — fierce power and the harm it inflicts; commonly the crushing chastisement or violent affliction that comes as a penalty.
11.grammar: A noun. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically links the word to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship (e.g. 'the might OF …') or appears after a preposition. It signals the word is being connected to or governed by something else.
11.root: ب-أ-س (b-ʾ-s) — might, hardship, distress, severe force

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
13.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

14.meaning: 'He/it came to us / reached us'. A past-tense verb of arriving or coming, here with 'us' as the ones reached.
14.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. With no added subject pronoun and the bare -a ending, it means 'he/it came' (third-person masculine singular, a completed action). The attached -nā is the object, 'us' — 'he came to us'.
14.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-') — to come, arrive

15.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
15.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
15.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

16.meaning: Pharaoh; the title/name of the ruler of ancient Egypt, used as a proper name.
16.grammar: A proper noun (a foreign name, which does not take nunation). The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence (the one doing the action).

17.meaning: A word meaning 'what' or 'that which' — a relative/indefinite particle pointing to an unspecified thing ('what', 'whatever', 'that which').
17.grammar: An invariable particle (mā) with no case ending. Depending on context it works as a relative pronoun ('that which') introducing a clause, or as an interrogative/indefinite ('what'). It does not inflect for case, gender, or number.

18.meaning: I show you / cause you to see — to make a group perceive or witness something, presenting it to their sight or understanding.
18.grammar: A present/imperfect Form IV (afʿala) verb, which here carries a causative sense, so it means 'to make (someone) see' = to show. The u- prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). The attached -kum means 'you all' as the object (those shown). It is in the indicative mood, the plain present-tense form for an ongoing or habitual action.

19.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
19.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

20.meaning: A word meaning 'what' or 'that which' — a relative/indefinite particle pointing to an unspecified thing ('what', 'whatever', 'that which').
20.grammar: An invariable particle (mā) with no case ending. Depending on context it works as a relative pronoun ('that which') introducing a clause, or as an interrogative/indefinite ('what'). It does not inflect for case, gender, or number.

21.meaning: A first-person singular present/future verb meaning 'I show / I make (someone) see' — this is the Form IV (causative) of 'to see', so it carries the sense of causing another to perceive or behold something, rather than the plain 'I see'.

parts.en: I (first-person prefix, on the Form IV causative)

21.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, first-person singular ('I ...'). It is built on the Form IV (causative) pattern of a weak root: the hamza/alif at the front does double duty here — it is both the first-person singular prefix and a reflex of the Form IV shape — while the weak final root letter surfaces as the long -ā.

22.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
22.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

23.meaning: I guide you / lead you — to direct a group toward the right way, showing them the path and steering them rightly.
23.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The a- prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). The attached -kum means 'you all' as the object (those guided). This is a defective (weak-final) verb whose third root letter is yāʾ; that yāʾ surfaces as the final -ī of the stem, and in this indicative form it is left unchanged ('I guide').

24.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
24.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

25.meaning: Way / path / road: a route taken, and by extension a course of conduct, means, or manner of life. 'Sabīl' is frequently used for a moral or spiritual road one travels.
25.grammar: A noun, 'way/path.' The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case — the case typically used for the direct object of a verb or for nouns governed in similar ways. Its definiteness comes from being joined to a following noun.

26.meaning: Right guidance, sound direction, rectitude — the way of correctness and maturity, the path that leads to what is right and well-guided.
26.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'). Its initial r- doubles because it is a 'sun letter' that absorbs the 'l' of al- in pronunciation. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship (e.g. 'the path OF …') or follows a preposition.
26.root: ر-ش-د (r-sh-d) — right guidance, sound judgment, maturity

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: 'He believed' — he had faith, trusted, and affirmed. The basic past-tense form of the verb meaning to believe and to find security in faith.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the root for security and faith. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he (believed)', stating a completed act of coming to faith.
3.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, trust, faith

4.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
4.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

5.meaning: 'Indeed I / truly I' — an emphasis particle ('verily, indeed') that strongly affirms a statement, fused with the attached pronoun 'I.'
5.grammar: The particle inna asserts and emphasizes the statement that follows ('indeed, truly, it is certainly the case that…'). It governs its noun in the accusative; that governed noun (the ism of inna) is the attached pronoun -ī, 'I/me,' which functions as the subject of the inna-clause. The predicate then follows. So inna here takes 'I' as its accusative-governed subject.
5.root: — (particle + pronoun, no triliteral root)

6.meaning: I fear, I am afraid of, I stand in awe/dread — expressing the speaker's own fear, whether dread of harm or reverent awe.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks the doer as 'I'. The final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual state ('I fear / I am fearing').

7.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
7.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

8.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'like,' 'similar to,' 'the equal of,' or 'a counterpart.' It expresses likeness or correspondence between things.
8.grammar: A noun in the accusative ending -a. This ending typically marks it as the object of a verb, as an adverbial 'in like manner,' or as the first term of a possessive link ('the like of …'). It conveys resemblance or equivalence to whatever it is paired with.
8.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similarity, comparison

9.meaning: 'Day' — a span of time. It denotes a day or a definite point/period of time; it links to a following word to specify which day (e.g., 'the day of …').
9.grammar: A masculine noun. Its final -i vowel is the genitive case: it typically appears after a preposition or when the word is linked to a following noun in an 'of …' relationship (as in 'the day OF …').

10.meaning: The factions / confederates / parties — groups banded together, especially allied bands or hostile coalitions. 'aḥzāb' is the plural of 'ḥizb', a party or group.
10.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural noun, 'the factions/parties'. The '-i' ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition or as the second term of an 'of' linkage ('... of the factions'). 'al-' means 'the'.

1.meaning: The like of / similar to; a match, equivalent, or counterpart — 'the same as' or 'something resembling.'
1.grammar: A noun meaning 'the like of.' The -a ending is the accusative case, the form typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) — so it points to 'the like (of something)' as what is involved in the action.

2.meaning: Habitual way, persistent practice, or recurring condition — a settled custom or manner that a people keep doing; the ongoing pattern or plight characteristic of them.
2.grammar: A noun. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically links the word to a following noun in an 'of' relationship (e.g. 'the way OF …') or comes after a preposition. It signals the word is connected to or governed by something else.
2.root: د-أ-ب (d-ʾ-b) — persistence, habitual effort, settled custom

3.meaning: A people, folk, or community — a group of persons bound together (often by kinship or shared identity); a nation or tribe.
3.grammar: A singular collective noun (grammatically masculine, referring to a group). The final -in is the genitive case with nunation (tanwīn), marking it indefinite ('a people'); the genitive typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('… of a people').
3.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, establish; a standing group of people

4.meaning: Noah — the proper name of the Prophet Nūḥ.
4.grammar: A proper name. The -in ending (nunation) shows it is treated as a fully declinable noun in the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or to link to a preceding word. (Most personal names are partly indeclinable, but this short name takes full case endings.)

5.meaning: And ʿĀd — the name of an ancient Arabian people (the nation of the prophet Hūd), proverbial for their power and their destruction after rejecting their messenger.
5.grammar: A proper name (a people) carrying the -in ending (indefinite genitive 'tanwīn'), the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). Here it takes regular case endings (it is 'fully inflected').
5.root: — (proper name)

6.meaning: And Thamūd — the name of an ancient Arabian people (the nation of the prophet Ṣāliḥ), known for carving homes in the rock and destroyed after rejecting their messenger.
6.grammar: A proper name (a people) with an -a ending and no 'tanwīn' (no final -n): it is 'diptote,' meaning it does not take the indefinite -n and uses -a for both the object and the after-preposition/linked positions. So this single -a form covers what would otherwise be two different case endings.

7.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
7.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
8.root: — (preposition)

9.meaning: "after them / following them" — the noun baʿd ('after, afterward') with the attached pronoun 'them', denoting what comes later in time than a group.
9.grammar: A time-noun used like a preposition, with an attached pronoun. The -i ending is genitive, the form taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive link. The suffix -him means 'them' (its vowel is -hi- to harmonise with the preceding -i).

10.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
11.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

12.meaning: He/it wills, wants, intends, desires — to seek or aim at something purposefully.
12.grammar: A present-tense (form IV) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he wills/wants'). The ya- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('does / is doing').
12.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, to want; (form IV) to will/intend

13.meaning: Wrongdoing, injustice, oppression — placing something where it does not belong; acting unjustly, whether against others, oneself, or the truth.
13.grammar: A noun. The final -an (accusative with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite and often as the object of a verb, or works adverbially ('wrongfully, unjustly'), describing the manner in which something is done.
13.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress, do injustice

14.meaning: For the servants (of Allah) — referring to human beings in their capacity as created, dependent beings entirely owned by and subservient to Allah.

parts.en: the — definite article (merged with the preposition)

14.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (for/to) takes a genitive noun, and when combined with the definite article 'al-', the two merge into 'lil-'. 'ʿibādi' is the genitive plural of 'ʿabd' (servant/slave), marked by the -i ending. The genitive is governed by the preceding preposition, indicating the beneficiaries or recipients.
14.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve; a servant or slave wholly devoted to another

1.meaning: 'And O my people!' — an affectionate call addressed to one's own community or kinsfolk.
1.grammar: A direct address: 'wa' ('and') plus the vocative particle 'yā' ('O') calling 'qawm' ('people'). The final -i stands in for the possessive 'my' (the 'ī' is shortened/dropped), so it means 'O my people'. 'qawm' is a collective term for one's community.
1.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group / community

2.meaning: 'Indeed I / truly I' — an emphasis particle ('verily, indeed') that strongly affirms a statement, fused with the attached pronoun 'I.'
2.grammar: The particle inna asserts and emphasizes the statement that follows ('indeed, truly, it is certainly the case that…'). It governs its noun in the accusative; that governed noun (the ism of inna) is the attached pronoun -ī, 'I/me,' which functions as the subject of the inna-clause. The predicate then follows. So inna here takes 'I' as its accusative-governed subject.

3.meaning: I fear, I am afraid of, I stand in awe/dread — expressing the speaker's own fear, whether dread of harm or reverent awe.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks the doer as 'I'. The final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual state ('I fear / I am fearing').
3.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — fear, fright, awe

4.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
4.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

5.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
5.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
5.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

6.meaning: The mutual calling out — the day when people will be calling to one another across vast distances, a vivid image of the chaos and cries of the Day of Resurrection.

parts.en: the mutual calling, calling out to one another

6.grammar: Verbal noun (masdar) of Form VI (tafāʿala pattern), which conveys reciprocal or mutual action between multiple parties — not just calling but calling back and forth. The root ن-د-و/ي is defective (final weak radical), so its Form VI masdar takes the defective pattern تَفَاعٍ (tafāʿin) rather than the sound tafāʿulun. In this form the final weak radical ي appears as the actual final letter; what looks like a genitive -i ending is in fact that weak radical ي surfacing in its kasra-supported position. The definite article renders the noun definite.
6.root: ن-د-و/ي (n-d-w/y) — to call, to summon, to cry out

1.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
1.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
1.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

2.meaning: You (all) turn away, turn your backs — to turn away from something, flee from it, or reverse one's direction, often used of turning away from faith or truth.

parts.en: you (plural) turn away / turn back (imperfect stem with plural marker)
the final -na suffix, the sign of the masculine plural in the imperfect indicative

2.grammar: Imperfect verb, second-person masculine plural, Form II or reflexive pattern, indicating the action of turning oneself. The ending '-ūna' (written as -ū + na) is the standard masculine plural imperfect indicative ending. This ending simultaneously marks: a plural subject (you all), present or future time, and the indicative mood (a straightforward statement or question, as opposed to the subjunctive -ū without na, or the jussive which also drops na).
2.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be close to; in derived forms, to turn, to take charge, or to turn away

3.meaning: Turning one's back, going away, retreating; people in the act of departing. This is the masculine plural active participle of 'to turn away', in the accusative/genitive form, often describing the manner in which people leave.
3.grammar: Active participle of a Form IV verb (ʾafʿala), following the mufʿil participle pattern, sound masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the accusative or genitive of a masculine plural; as an accusative it commonly functions as a circumstantial description ('while turning away').
3.root: د-ب-ر (d-b-r) — the back, hind part; to turn the back, to go away

4.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

5.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

6.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
6.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
8.root: — (preposition)

9.meaning: 'Protector / defender / one who shields and saves from harm' — an active participle for someone or something that guards and rescues.
9.grammar: An active participle ('one who protects') in the genitive indefinite, marked by -in (tanwīn). The genitive here typically follows a preposition or a negation construction ('not… any protector').

10.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
10.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

11.meaning: He lets/leads astray — he causes someone to lose the right way, leaving them to wander from guidance.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he …'), in the causative pattern ('to cause to stray'). It stands in the jussive/conditional mood (the doubled lām broken apart and given a helping -i to ease pronunciation), typically meaning 'whomever he lets stray …'.
11.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
12.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
12.root: — (proper divine name)

13.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
13.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

14.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
14.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

15.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
15.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
15.root: — (preposition)

16.meaning: A guide — one who shows the way, leads to the right path, or directs others toward what is correct. The indefinite form conveys 'any guide' or 'a guide (at all)'.
16.grammar: An active participle ('one who guides'). It belongs to the class of nouns ending in a weak letter, so the indefinite tanwīn shows up as -in. This -in marks it as indefinite and signals nominative/genitive case: 'a guide'.
16.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, direct

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: "he/it came to you" — a past verb "came" with the pronoun "you" as the one reached, i.e. something arrived at or reached a group of people.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base third-person masculine singular form ("he/it came"), with no extra subject suffix. The verb "to come" is intransitive, so the attached -kum is not a direct object but an indirect (dative) pronoun — "to you" (masculine plural), equivalent to "came to you (all)."

3.meaning: Yūsuf (Joseph), the proper name of the Prophet. A non-Arabic personal name.
3.grammar: A proper name that is diptote (it does not take tanwīn and resists the normal -i for genitive). The final -u is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the one being named/spoken about.
3.root: — (proper name; non-Arabic origin)

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
5.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
5.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

6.meaning: 'With the clear proofs / evident signs' — bayyināt are plain, self-evident demonstrations that make the truth manifest, leaving no doubt.
6.grammar: Built from 'bi-' ('with/by means of') + 'al-' ('the') + a feminine plural noun meaning 'clear proofs.' The -i ending is the genitive case, required after the preposition 'bi-'; the feminine sound plural '-āt' takes -i (not -a) in this case. The whole phrase means 'with the clear proofs.'

7.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
7.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

8.meaning: You (all) ceased, you did not stop — the past-tense form used in the construction 'mā ziltum', meaning 'you kept on doing something' or 'you never stopped'; the base verb expresses the continuity or cessation of a state.

parts.en: you (plural) — second-person masculine plural perfect suffix

8.grammar: Perfect (past) tense verb, second-person masculine plural, from the hollow verb 'zāla' (weak middle radical و). Hollow verbs have a long vowel in place of the middle radical; when a consonantal suffix such as '-tum' is added, the middle radical elides and the preceding vowel shortens, producing 'zil-tum'. The suffix '-tum' is the standard masculine plural perfect marker. This verb functions as a sister of 'kāna' (a verb of being/continuity) and is almost always used with a negative particle ('mā ziltum' = 'you never ceased / you kept on'). It does not carry a nominal case ending since it is a verb.
8.root: ز-و-ل (z-w-l) — to cease, to move away from, to stop being in a state

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

10.meaning: 'Doubt / uncertainty.' A noun for the wavering state of mind in which one is unsure and cannot settle on what is true — the opposite of firm certainty.
10.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('a doubt / some doubt'). The genitive -i is the form taken after a preposition — typically conveying 'in doubt' or 'of doubt.'
10.root: ش-ك-ك (sh-k-k) — to doubt, be uncertain, waver

11.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
11.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

12.meaning: "he/it came to you" — a past verb "came" with the pronoun "you" as the one reached, i.e. something arrived at or reached a group of people.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base third-person masculine singular form ("he/it came"), with no extra subject suffix. The verb "to come" is intransitive, so the attached -kum is not a direct object but an indirect (dative) pronoun — "to you" (masculine plural), equivalent to "came to you (all)."
12.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, arrive

13.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
13.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

14.meaning: A particle meaning 'until / up to the point that / so that finally'. It marks an end-limit in time or place, or the goal at which an action culminates.
