14.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case endings and never changes form). It introduces the end-point or purpose of what precedes, and when followed by a verb it can give the sense of 'until' or 'so that'.

15.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
15.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.
15.root: — (a time particle; no triliteral root)

16.meaning: Means 'he perished / died / passed away.' It denotes a person's death, and more broadly the perishing, ruin, or coming-to-an-end of something.
16.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in its base form, marking a completed action. The shape with the final '-a' carries a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') with no added prefix or suffix — the bare perfect verb already means 'he did.'

17.meaning: 'You (plural) said' — to say, speak, or utter. The verb covers any act of stating or declaring something in words.
17.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The suffix -tum marks the masculine plural 'you (all)' as the doers of a completed action — it signals both the past tense and that the speakers being addressed are a group. (This is a hollow verb: its middle root letter is a wāw, which surfaces as a long ā in the base form qāla but reduces to a short u, giving qul-, before a consonant-initial suffix like -tum.)
17.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

18.meaning: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
18.grammar: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.

19.meaning: That He raise up, rouse, or send forth — to stir something into action and dispatch it, or to raise the dead to life.
19.grammar: Present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'); the final -a is the subjunctive mood, the form used after particles like 'that' or 'so that' to express purpose or a dependent action.
19.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to raise up, rouse, send forth

20.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
20.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

21.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
21.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

22.meaning: 'After him / it' — 'baʿd' denotes what comes afterward in time or sequence, here joined to 'him/it'.
22.grammar: A time-noun 'baʿd' (afterness) with an attached pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. The '-i' vowel on 'baʿd' is its case ending, set by 'baʿd's' own position in the sentence (commonly governed by a preceding preposition), not by the suffix; the attached '-hi' is the possessor ('him/it'), and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive. The pronoun's 'i'-vowel (-hi rather than -hu) follows because it comes after a genitive '-i'.

23.meaning: "a messenger / an envoy" — one who is sent bearing a message; 'rasūl' is an emissary commissioned to convey something on behalf of the one who sent him, especially a prophet sent with a divine message.
23.grammar: A masculine noun on the faʿūl pattern, indefinite ('a messenger'). The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥ) is the indefinite accusative case, the form used for the direct object of a verb; the written alif carries this ending.
23.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message, messenger

24.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
24.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
24.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

25.meaning: A verb meaning 'he leads astray' or 'he lets go astray' — to cause someone to lose the right way, to misguide or allow to wander from the correct path.
25.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the causative (form IV) pattern. The yu- prefix marks third-person singular with the vowel typical of derived causative verbs, and the final -u marks the indicative mood (ongoing or habitual action). The causative pattern gives the sense of 'causing to go astray'.
25.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, err

26.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
26.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

27.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
27.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

28.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
28.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

29.meaning: One who is excessive, extravagant, or wasteful — a person who oversteps proper limits, squandering or going to harmful extremes. Often used of transgressing the bounds Allah has set.

parts.en: one who is excessive / a transgressor of limits

29.grammar: An active participle of the Form IV (afʿala) pattern, naming the doer: 'one who commits excess'. The final -un is the indefinite nominative ending: it marks an indefinite noun ('a …') that serves as the subject of a sentence or as the main predicate describing the subject.
29.root: س-ر-ف (s-r-f) — exceeding the proper limit, excess, waste

30.meaning: One who is in doubt, a doubter — a person who harbors deep uncertainty and suspicion, especially regarding divine truth or the signs of Allah.

parts.en: a doubter, one who is suspicious or uncertain

30.grammar: Active participle of Form VIII (iftiʿāl pattern, here irtāba — 'to be doubtful, to suspect'). It is masculine singular with the -un ending (tanwīn ḍamma), marking it as indefinite and in the nominative case. The nominative is the case of the subject of a sentence or the predicate of a nominal sentence.

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'they dispute, argue, or contend with one another'; it carries the sense of pressing an argument back and forth, wrangling and quarreling, often persistently and in opposition to truth.
2.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The -jādil- stem is a Form III pattern signaling mutual, reciprocal action — arguing against an opponent. The -ūna ending marks 'they (men/people)' in the indicative mood, the plain-statement form; were a governing particle present, this would shorten to -ū.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
3.root: — (particle)

4.meaning: Signs / verses / evidentiary marks — the plural of 'āyah', a sign or token that points to something beyond itself; used for miraculous signs, natural wonders, and the discrete verses of revelation.
4.grammar: A sound feminine plural. The '-in' (nunation) ending marks it as indefinite ('signs', not 'the signs') and is the genitive/accusative (oblique) case form, typical of an object or a word governed by a preposition.
4.root: ا-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token that indicates something

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
6.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
6.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

7.meaning: 'Authority, warrant, sanction' — a proof or sanctioning power that gives one the right to make a claim; can mean compelling evidence or delegated authority/dominion.
7.grammar: A noun. The '-in' (tanwīn kasra) marks it indefinite ('any authority/proof') and in the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or in an 'of' linkage. It commonly denotes both a sanctioning proof and ruling power.

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'it/he came to them, reached them, arrived to them,' with the object 'them.' The root sense is coming or arriving at a destination.

parts.en: them / to them (attached object pronoun, masculine plural)

8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it came'), with a weak final root-letter showing as the long -ā. The attached -hum is the object pronoun, 'them' (a male group). The action is viewed as completed.
8.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, reach

9.meaning: A finite past-tense verb meaning 'it became great/weighty/burdensome' — that something grew large, heavy, hard to bear, or oppressive to the heart. Often used of a matter felt as overwhelming or intolerably difficult.
9.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The intransitive vowel pattern (-u- in the middle) indicates an inherent quality — it 'is/became' great rather than acting on something. The final -a is the standard ending of this past-tense form.

10.meaning: Intense hatred, loathing — a deep, active revulsion or abhorrence, often describing the intense hatred that Allah has for something morally repugnant.

parts.en: intense hatred, deep loathing (accusative with tanwīn)

10.grammar: Masculine singular noun with double fatḥa tanwīn (-an), marking it as indefinite and in the accusative case. The accusative signals it functions as a verbal intensifier (cognate accusative, mafʿūl muṭlaq), amplifying the meaning of an accompanying verb — expressing that the action is done 'greatly' or 'intensely'. It can also serve as the object expressing disdain.
10.root: م-ق-ت (m-q-t) — to hate intensely, to despise, to abhor

11.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
11.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: The compound 'and with / and in the presence of' — the connector 'and' joined to a word meaning 'with, near, in the presence of, in the sight of'. This locational/possessive term points to something being held, present, or reckoned in someone's estimation.

parts.en: with, near, in the presence of

13.grammar: The connective 'and' (wa-) prefixed to the locational word ʿinda. ʿinda is an adverb of place/possession ('with, at, in the presence of') that always stands in the accusative-looking form ending in -a and is followed by a noun or pronoun it relates to, giving 'with/in the sight of …'.
13.root: — (no triliteral verbal root; ʿinda is a locational particle)

14.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
14.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

15.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
15.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
15.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

16.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
16.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
16.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

17.meaning: He sets a stamp/seal — to impress a mark; spiritually, to seal a heart so it is closed to truth. The 'he' can refer to Allah or stand for an impersonal 'it is sealed'.
17.grammar: Present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks the third person 'he' or 'it'. The final -u is the plain indicative ending, marking an ordinary present ('he seals / he is sealing').

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
18.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

19.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
19.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

20.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
20.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

21.meaning: Heart — the innermost core of a person; in the Qur'anic worldview, the heart is the seat of understanding, faith, intention, and moral perception, not merely an emotion.
21.grammar: Masculine singular noun in the genitive case, marked by the -i ending. The genitive arises from a construct (iḍāfa) with a following possessive pronoun or noun, expressing 'the heart of …'. The word has no definite article; definiteness comes from what follows in the construct chain.
21.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over, to flip; the heart is so named for its constant turning

22.meaning: 'An arrogant one / a haughty person' — one who magnifies himself, swelling with self-importance and looking down on others. The form names someone who actively makes himself out to be greater than he is.
22.grammar: An active participle of the 'self-magnifying' stem ('one who makes himself great'). The -in ending marks it as indefinite ('an arrogant one') and in the genitive state — typically following a preposition or linked to a preceding noun. The mu- prefix identifies the doer of the action.
22.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great; (this stem) to be arrogant, haughty

23.meaning: An intensive noun/adjective meaning 'a tyrant, an overbearing oppressor' — one who is haughty and compels others by force, arrogant and domineering. (The same root word can describe a restorer/mender, but in the human-descriptive sense it denotes overbearing arrogance.)
23.grammar: An intensive noun on the faʿʿāl pattern, denoting one who does something habitually or to a high degree. The final -in is the genitive case with nunation (indefinite); this ending typically appears after a preposition or when the word follows and qualifies another genitive noun.
23.root: ج-ب-ر (j-b-r) — to compel, force; also to set/mend

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: Pharaoh; the title/name of the ruler of ancient Egypt, used as a proper name.
2.grammar: A proper noun (a foreign name, which does not take nunation). The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence (the one doing the action).

3.meaning: O Haman. A vocative address to Haman, Pharaoh's chief minister, ordering him to construct the tower.
3.grammar: Yā is the vocative particle. Hāmān is a proper noun (diptote), here in the nominative form used for proper names in vocative constructions.

4.meaning: 'Son (of)' — a male child or descendant; commonly used to link a person to their father or lineage.
4.grammar: A singular masculine noun meaning 'son.' The '-i' ending is genitive — the state a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a following noun ('son OF …'). This word characteristically stands between two names, joining a person to his father in a chain of descent.
4.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w / b-n-y) — son, offspring; to build

5.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
5.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

6.meaning: a lofty tower / a tall building. Ṣarḥ refers to a high, imposing structure — a palace or tower of great height.

parts.en: a lofty tower, a tall palace, a high structure (accusative indefinite)

6.grammar: Masculine noun in the accusative case (manṣūb), indicated by -an (tanwīn with fatḥa). Object of the preceding imperative.
6.root: ص-ر-ح (ṣ-r-ḥ) — a lofty building, a palace tower; to be manifest, exposed

7.meaning: An expression of hope or expectation introducing a clause, meaning roughly 'so that perhaps I…' or 'in the hope that I…'. It combines the particle laʿalla ('perhaps / it may be that', used to express a hoped-for or anticipated outcome) with the attached 'I' pronoun, conveying that the speaker hopes or expects to do something.
7.grammar: laʿalla is a particle of hope or expectation that takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject (its ism) in the accusative and a predicate in the nominative. The attached -ī is that first-person singular subject pronoun ('I'), held in the accusative as the ism of laʿalla, so the whole means 'perhaps I…'.

8.meaning: I reach, I attain — to arrive at, to reach a destination or a goal, conveying the sense of ascending to or accessing something.

parts.en: I reach, I attain (first-person singular imperfect indicative)

8.grammar: Imperfect verb, first-person singular, Form I, in the indicative mood. The final -u (ḍamma on the ghain) is the indicative mood marker for the imperfect. The indicative signals a plain statement of action — 'I (do) reach' — as opposed to the subjunctive (-a) or jussive (no vowel). The prefix a- marks the first-person singular in the imperfect.
8.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, to attain, to arrive at

9.meaning: The pathways, the means, the routes — literally 'the causes' or 'the ropes', referring to the means or passages that allow access to something, used of the avenues leading to the heavens.

parts.en: the pathways, means, causes (definite accusative plural)

9.grammar: Masculine plural noun with the definite article. 'Asbāb' is a broken plural of 'sabab', following the أَفعَال (afʿāl) broken-plural template — not a sound plural (sound masculine plurals end in -ūn/-īn; sound feminine plurals end in -āt). The -a ending (fatḥa without tanwīn) marks the accusative case for this definite noun. The accusative signals this word is the direct object of a preceding verb. In extended usage 'asbāb' refers to any means, ropes, or paths of access.
9.root: س-ب-ب (s-b-b) — a rope, a cause, a means of connection or access

1.meaning: The pathways, the means — same core meaning as the definite form above: the routes, rungs, or means of access. Appearing in a construct with what follows.
1.grammar: Masculine broken plural noun (afʿāl pattern) without the definite article, carrying the -a (fatḥa) ending. When a noun stands in the first position of a construct (iḍāfa), it loses the definite article and its tanwīn; definiteness is supplied by the following genitive noun (e.g., 'the pathways OF the heavens'). The fatḥa here is the accusative ending, functioning as the object of a preceding verb.
1.root: س-ب-ب (s-b-b) — a rope, a cause, a means of connection or access

2.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
2.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

3.meaning: So that I may look, so that I may peer — to look up toward, to gaze at from below seeking to perceive something distant or elevated.

parts.en: I may look up at, I may peer (subjunctive, first-person singular, Form VIII)

3.grammar: The particle 'fa-' introduces a consequence or purpose. 'Aṭṭaliʿa' is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive mood, first-person singular, Form VIII (iftiʿāl) of the root ط-ل-ع. In Form VIII the infix ت assimilates to the emphatic ط of this root, yielding the doubled ط (اِطَّلَعَ / يَطَّلِعُ). The subjunctive -a ending (as opposed to the indicative -u) signals purpose or a potential action following a preceding verb — 'so that I may look'.
3.root: ط-ل-ع (ṭ-l-ʿ) — to rise, to ascend, to look up at, to come upon

4.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
4.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

5.meaning: (the) God / the deity. Ilāh refers to a god or deity — the object of worship. Here used in the construct state ('the God of Moses').
5.grammar: Masculine noun in the genitive case (majrūr), -i (kasra) ending, in an iḍāfa construction ('God of…').
5.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — deity, god; ilāh: the one worshipped

6.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
6.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

7.meaning: And indeed I — a connector 'and' joined to an emphatic particle that strongly affirms what follows ('truly, indeed'), with 'I' attached as its subject.
7.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the emphatic particle inna, which lends strong certainty to the statement it opens. The attached -ī ('me/I') is its grammatical subject; inna places the noun or pronoun after it in the accusative.

8.meaning: [I] think that he / I indeed suppose he (is). Refers to Pharaoh's assertion of certainty through conjecture — making a strong claim based on assumption.

parts.en: I think, I assume, I conjecture (Form I, 1st singular)

8.grammar: Present-tense verb (mudāriʿ), 1st person singular, Form I (ẓanna — to think, to suppose). The emphatic lām precedes for strong assertion. -hu is the attached object pronoun.
8.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to think, to suppose; ẓann: conjecture, supposition

9.meaning: A liar — one who speaks falsehood, who says what is untrue. As an active participle it describes a person characterized by lying.
9.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word on the fāʿil pattern, فَاعِل, meaning 'one who does X') used as a noun or description: 'a lying one, a liar'. The final -an is the indefinite accusative ending: it marks an indefinite noun ('a …') that is functioning as an object or as a predicate/description.

10.meaning: 'And likewise / and in the same way / and thus' — a connective phrase pointing back to a manner just mentioned and saying 'in that very way…'. Built from 'and' + 'like' + 'that'.
10.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'; the prefix ka- means 'like/as'; 'dhālika' is the demonstrative 'that' (pointing to something distant or already mentioned). Because ka- acts like a preposition, the word after it stands in the genitive, though the demonstrative 'dhālika' keeps a fixed form and shows no visible case change. The whole means 'and just like that / and thus'.

11.meaning: It was made beautiful / adorned / made alluring; the act of decorating something or making it appear attractive and appealing.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice on an intensive (form II) pattern, so the action is done to the subject and stresses thorough adorning ("was made beautiful/alluring"). The -u-…-i- vowel pattern marks the passive, and the final -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject ("it/he").

12.meaning: To Pharaoh — the preposition 'to' plus the proper name Firʿawn (Pharaoh), the title of the Egyptian ruler in the Quranic narrative.
12.grammar: The preposition li- governs the genitive. Firʿawn is a non-Arabic proper name that takes a fatḥa in all cases in Classical Arabic (diptoton / non-fully declinable noun).

13.meaning: "evil / badness of" — that which is bad, harmful, or offensive; the wrongness or foulness of a thing. In the construct form it means 'the evil of …'.
13.grammar: A noun meaning 'evil/badness'. The final -u is the nominative case, the case used for a subject or for the thing being asserted. The bare (non-tanwīn) ending shows it is in a construct (possessive) chain, leaning on a following noun: 'the evil OF …'.
13.root: س-و-أ (s-w-') — to be bad, to harm, to do evil; that which displeases

14.meaning: His deed, his action — a specific act or work performed, carrying the sense of a volitional, effortful act with moral consequence.

parts.en: his — third-person masculine singular possessive pronoun suffix

14.grammar: Masculine singular noun in the genitive case, marked by the -i ending, standing as the second term of a construct that began with 'sūʾu' (the evil of). The possessive suffix '-hi' ('his') is attached, further specifying whose deed is meant. The genitive is expected as the second element of an iḍāfa construction.
14.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, to act, to work; an 'amal is a deliberate deed

15.meaning: And he was turned away, and he was barred — to be repelled or deflected from something, implying that someone or something was blocked and prevented from a path or a truth.

parts.en: he was turned away, he was blocked (third-person masculine singular perfect passive)

15.grammar: The conjunction 'wa' joins this to a preceding clause. 'Ṣudda' is a perfect (past) tense verb in the passive voice, third-person masculine singular. In Arabic, the passive of Form I is formed by changing the vowel pattern to u-i (ḍamma on the first syllable, kasra on the second); the -a ending on the final letter is the standard perfect third-person masculine singular marker. The passive voice indicates the subject was acted upon — someone or something caused the blocking.
15.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to bar, to block, to turn someone away from a path

16.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
16.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

17.meaning: The way, road, or path — a route one travels; very often used figuratively for a course of life, conduct, or the path of religion. The attached article makes it definite: 'the way'.
17.grammar: al- is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates to the following 's', heard as 'as-sabīl'). The final -i is the genitive ending, marking the word as joined to a preceding noun ('… OF the way') or governed by a preposition.

18.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
18.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

19.meaning: A scheme / a plot / a cunning stratagem — a carefully devised plan, often with a connotation of guile or trickery aimed at another.
19.grammar: A noun. The -u ending is the nominative case, typically marking it as the subject or the thing being spoken about. It is also commonly the first term of an 'of' phrase (e.g., 'the scheme of …').
19.root: ك-ي-د (k-y-d) — to plot, scheme, contrive a stratagem

20.meaning: Pharaoh — the title/name of the ruler of ancient Egypt, used as a proper name for that figure.
20.grammar: A proper name. Being a foreign, non-inflecting (diptote) name, it takes a single -a for both the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn. Here it follows another noun in a possessive link ('… of Pharaoh').

21.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
21.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

22.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
22.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

23.meaning: Utter ruin, perdition, destruction — the state of being completely ruined and brought to nothing.
23.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar) from the root t-b-b, appearing as an indefinite masculine noun. The final -in ending is the nunation (tanwīn) on the kasra, marking the word as indefinite and in the genitive case — genitive typically follows a preposition or a preceding noun in a possessive (iḍāfa) construction. Indefinite nunation signals that the word is used in a general, unspecified sense ('a ruin', 'utter ruin').

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: 'He believed' — he had faith, trusted, and affirmed. The basic past-tense form of the verb meaning to believe and to find security in faith.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the root for security and faith. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he (believed)', stating a completed act of coming to faith.
3.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, trust, faith

4.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
4.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

5.meaning: Follow me! — a command to follow or obey the speaker, with an attached first-person object pronoun ('me').

parts.en: me (attached first-person object pronoun, shortened form)

5.grammar: A Form VIII (iftiʿāl) imperative verb, second person masculine plural, from the root t-b-ʿ ('to follow'). The -ū ending marks the plural masculine imperative ('you all, follow'). The attached -ni is the first-person singular object pronoun ('me'), shortened from -nī in connected speech (the final yā' is dropped before a pause or as a variant form). Together the form means 'Follow me!'
5.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, to come after, to obey

6.meaning: I will guide you (plural) — the speaker will show, direct, or lead the addressed group to a path or goal.

parts.en: I will guide / let me guide (first-person imperfect or hortative)

6.grammar: An imperfect (mudāriʿ) verb in the first-person singular, Form I, from the root h-d-y. The a- prefix marks first-person singular. The -i on the stem reflects the jussive or shortened form (majzūm/amr context, losing the final -ī), often used after an invitation or conditional clause. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object pronoun ('you all'). Together: 'I will guide you (all)'.
6.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, to show the way, to lead aright

7.meaning: Way / path / road: a route taken, and by extension a course of conduct, means, or manner of life. 'Sabīl' is frequently used for a moral or spiritual road one travels.
7.grammar: A noun, 'way/path.' The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case — the case typically used for the direct object of a verb or for nouns governed in similar ways. Its definiteness comes from being joined to a following noun.

8.meaning: Right guidance, sound direction, rectitude — the way of correctness and maturity, the path that leads to what is right and well-guided.
8.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'). Its initial r- doubles because it is a 'sun letter' that absorbs the 'l' of al- in pronunciation. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship (e.g. 'the path OF …') or follows a preposition.
8.root: ر-ش-د (r-sh-d) — right guidance, sound judgment, maturity

1.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
1.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
1.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

2.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
2.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

3.meaning: This (feminine) — a pointing word ('this one here') used for a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
3.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand. It is fixed in form and does not change for case; it commonly precedes the noun it points to.

4.meaning: 'The life' — earthly existence, the span of living in this world. The word denotes life as the state of being alive, vitality, and the worldly life as a whole.
4.grammar: 'al-' is the definite article 'the'. The final '-u' is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence (the one doing or being something), or as the predicate naming what something is.

5.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
5.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
5.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

6.meaning: Provision, enjoyment, or maintenance; a beneficial gift of goods, comfort, or sustenance that one is given to make use of, typically for a limited time.
6.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamm) marks the indefinite nominative — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for the thing being stated to exist ('there is a provision').
6.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — to provide enjoyment/benefit; goods, comfort

7.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
7.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

8.meaning: A noun meaning 'the Hereafter / the next life / the world to come' — literally 'the last (abode)', the final, everlasting existence following this present life.
8.grammar: A definite noun (al- = 'the') bearing the -a ending, which marks the accusative (object) case — the form a noun takes when it is the object of a verb. It is feminine in form (the tā' marbūṭa ending).
8.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after; lastness, the end

9.meaning: A standalone pronoun meaning 'she' or 'it' (feminine). Arabic has no neuter, so 'it' for a feminine noun is expressed with this word. Used independently for emphasis or to stand as the subject of a sentence.
9.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person feminine singular. It stands on its own (not attached to another word) and most often functions as the subject of a nominal sentence ('she/it is …'). Its form is fixed and does not take case endings.

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'abode', 'dwelling', or 'home' — a place of residence and settling; used for a lasting dwelling-place, including the eternal Hereafter.
10.grammar: A noun bearing the -u (nominative) ending, which typically marks it as the subject of a sentence or the predicate in a statement of identity ('X will be the abode'). It frequently heads a possessive phrase ('the abode OF …').
10.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn, encircle; a dwelling enclosed by walls

11.meaning: Permanent settlement, stable abode — the state or place of final rest and lasting dwelling, as opposed to a temporary stop.
11.grammar: A definite masculine noun in the genitive case, indicated by the kasra ending -i. The genitive case shows the noun is in a possessive or descriptive relation with a preceding noun (typically in an iḍāfa construction, e.g. 'the home OF settlement'). The definite article al- makes it specific — 'the (true, final) permanent abode'.
11.root: ق-ر-ر (q-r-r) — to settle, to be firm/stable; a resting place, permanence

1.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
1.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

2.meaning: 'He did / worked / acted' — to perform a deed or action, to do work.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base form. With no added subject-suffix and the final -a, it carries the default third-person masculine singular subject, 'he did'. The past tense presents the action as completed.

3.meaning: An evil (deed) / a wrong — something bad, harmful, or sinful; a misdeed or its grievous result. The opposite of a good deed.
3.grammar: A feminine noun (built on the pattern of an intensive adjective used as a noun, 'a bad thing'). The '-an' ending (on the feminine '-at-') is indefinite accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb.
3.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad, evil, harmful

4.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
4.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

5.meaning: 'He / it will be recompensed, repaid, requited' — the passive of the verb meaning to be given a fitting return for one's deeds. The subject is the one receiving the recompense, not the one giving it.
5.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the passive voice, third-person masculine singular ('he/it is/will be …'). The yu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks the passive, so the subject is the receiver of the action ('is repaid') rather than the doer. Built on the root for repaying in kind.
5.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — recompense, requital, repaying in kind

6.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
6.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

7.meaning: 'Its / her like, the equal of it' — the singular noun mithl ('a like, a counterpart, an equivalent') with an attached possessive 'its/her,' denoting something matching or comparable to a thing.
7.grammar: A singular noun ('a like/equal') with the possessive suffix -hā ('its/her'). The -a ending marks the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb or in an adverb-like sense ('to the like of it'). The suffix -hā refers to a feminine or non-human owner.

8.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
8.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
8.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

9.meaning: 'He did / worked / acted' — to perform a deed or action, to do work.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base form. With no added subject-suffix and the final -a, it carries the default third-person masculine singular subject, 'he did'. The past tense presents the action as completed.

10.meaning: "Righteous / good / sound" — an active participle describing one who or that which is upright and wholesome and acts rightly; as a description of deeds it means good, virtuous works.
10.grammar: An active participle used as a noun or adjective. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a righteous one / a good deed') and in the accusative case — the form used for a direct object or other complement.
10.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound / upright / righteous

11.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
11.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

12.meaning: 'A male' — a noun denoting a male, of human beings or animals.

parts.en: genitive ('-in') ending with tanwīn marking it indefinite

12.grammar: A singular noun. The ending -in is the genitive case with tanwīn ('a/an'): it marks the word as indefinite and typically links it to a preceding noun or follows a preposition ('… OF a male').
12.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — maleness; (also) to remember, mention

13.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
13.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

14.meaning: A female — a female being, whether human or animal; the counterpart of 'male'.
14.grammar: A singular noun denoting a female. It ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case, so its grammatical role is shown by context rather than by a final vowel.
14.root: ا-ن-ث (ʾ-n-th) — femaleness, the female

15.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
15.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

16.meaning: An active participle / noun meaning 'a believer' — one who has faith, who trusts and affirms; literally 'one who makes/declares secure'.
16.grammar: Active participle (form IV) used as a noun, masculine singular, indefinite. The final -un (tanwīn ḍamma) is the indefinite nominative, which typically marks the word as the subject of a clause or the thing being identified.

17.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
17.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.

18.meaning: 'they enter' — to go into or pass inside a place.
18.grammar: A present/future verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they …'). The ending -ūna combines the plural 'they' (-ū) with the indicative marker -na, signalling a simple ongoing or future statement. The ya- prefix marks the third person.
18.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, go in, penetrate

19.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — the place of lush, shaded greenery promised as the abode of bliss; literally a garden whose foliage covers the ground.
19.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. 'janna' is a feminine noun (the tā marbūṭa ending). The final -a is accusative, the form typically marking a word as the object of a verb or, with place-nouns, the destination/location toward which an action occurs.

20.meaning: They are given provision / sustained — to be granted 'rizq': the provision, sustenance, and bounty that Allah bestows (food, livelihood, and every good thing).
20.grammar: A present/imperfect passive verb (Form I): the 'yu-' prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks it passive ('are given/provided'), so the doer is unstated. The '-ūna' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject and the indicative mood (ongoing/general action, not negated or subordinated).

21.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
21.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

22.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
22.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
22.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

23.meaning: 'Reckoning / account / measure'. It refers to counting, calculating, or taking account — and by extension a limit or measure derived from counting. Often used of a tally or the act of holding to account.
23.grammar: The '-in' ending (tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('a reckoning / any measure') and in the genitive case. The genitive typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

1.meaning: 'And O my people!' — an affectionate call addressed to one's own community or kinsfolk.
1.grammar: A direct address: 'wa' ('and') plus the vocative particle 'yā' ('O') calling 'qawm' ('people'). The final -i stands in for the possessive 'my' (the 'ī' is shortened/dropped), so it means 'O my people'. 'qawm' is a collective term for one's community.
1.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group / community

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
3.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

4.meaning: I call you (plural) — the speaker is summoning, inviting, or calling out to the addressed group, typically toward belief, guidance, or a cause.

parts.en: I call / I invite (first-person singular imperfect)

4.grammar: An imperfect (mudāriʿ) verb, Form I, first-person singular, from the defective (nāqiṣ) root d-ʿ-w — defective because the wāw is the final radical (lām al-fiʿl), not the middle one. The a- prefix marks first person; the stem -dʿū retains the wāw as a long vowel in the imperfect indicative. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object pronoun ('you all'). Together: 'I call/invite you all'. The imperfect tense describes an ongoing or habitual action.
4.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, to invite, to summon, to supplicate

5.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
5.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

6.meaning: Salvation, deliverance — being rescued or saved from harm, destruction, or punishment; escape to safety.
6.grammar: A definite feminine noun in the genitive case, indicated by the kasra ending -i (the tā' marbūṭa of the base form najāh is opened to -t- before the genitive vowel). The genitive case shows this noun follows a preposition or is the second term of a possessive construction — 'to salvation', 'of salvation'. The definite article specifies a particular, complete salvation.
6.root: ن-ج-و / ن-ج-ي (n-j-w / n-j-y) — to save, to escape, to be delivered

7.meaning: While you (plural) call me — the addressed group is simultaneously or contrarily calling the speaker (toward something), used to set up a contrast with what the speaker calls them to.

parts.en: you (plural) call / invite (second-person masculine plural imperfect)
me (first-person singular object pronoun — nūn al-wiqāya + yā')

7.grammar: The verb tadʿūna is an imperfect second-person masculine plural form from the defective root d-ʿ-w. The ta- prefix marks second person; the -ūna ending marks masculine plural indicative mood. The attached -nī is the full first-person singular object pronoun ('me'), comprising nūn al-wiqāya (the protective nūn) and the yā' pronoun — both are present and unshortened in this form. The wāw prefix is a coordinating conjunction meaning 'and' or 'while', signalling contrast or simultaneity with a preceding clause.
7.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, to invite, to summon, to supplicate

8.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
8.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

9.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
9.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

1.meaning: You (plural) call me — the addressed group calls or invites the speaker (toward something, often disbelief or false worship); a statement of what they do.

parts.en: me (first-person singular object pronoun — nūn al-wiqāya + yā')

1.grammar: Identical in morphology to id 431 but without the wa- prefix. An imperfect second-person masculine plural verb from the defective root d-ʿ-w; ta- marks second person, -ūna marks masculine plural indicative. The suffix -nī is the full first-person singular object pronoun, consisting of nūn al-wiqāya and the yā' pronoun, both present and unshortened. The indicative -ūna indicates a simple declarative statement about an ongoing or habitual action: 'You (all) call me'.
1.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, to invite, to summon, to supplicate

2.meaning: That I disbelieve — the act of rejecting, denying, or being ungrateful; covering over the truth. Kufr encompasses disbelief in Allah, rejection of His messengers, and ingratitude for His blessings.

parts.en: that / in order that (lām of purpose, introducing subjunctive)
I disbelieve / I reject (first-person singular subjunctive)

2.grammar: The lī- prefix is the lām of purpose or causation, which requires the following verb to be in the subjunctive (manṣūb) mood. The verb akfura is Form I imperfect, first-person singular, in the subjunctive — indicated by the fatḥa ending -a instead of the indicative -u. The a- prefix marks first person. Together: 'that I should disbelieve / in order for me to disbelieve'.
2.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to disbelieve, to reject, to be ungrateful; covering over the truth

3.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
3.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
3.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

4.meaning: And that I associate (partners with Allah) — the act of shirk, ascribing partners, equals, or rivals to Allah, which is the gravest sin in Islamic theology.

parts.en: I associate (partners) / I commit shirk (first-person singular subjunctive, Form IV)

4.grammar: The wa- is a coordinating conjunction linking this clause to a preceding purpose clause. The verb ush'rika is Form IV (ifʿāl), which here has a causative or factitive meaning — 'to make something a partner, to ascribe partnership'. First-person singular, subjunctive mood, indicated by the fatḥa ending -a (governed by the lām of purpose from a preceding clause). The u- prefix of Form IV imperfect marks first person in this measure.
4.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, to partner; to associate partners with Allah (shirk)

5.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not'. Unlike a simple particle, it behaves like a verb (frozen in the past-tense form) and serves to deny that something is the case, cancelling an assertion of being.
7.grammar: A defective verb fixed in the 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'). The final -a is its frozen ending; it does not conjugate for tense like other verbs. Grammatically it raises its subject to the nominative and puts its predicate in the accusative, functioning to negate a state of being.

8.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
8.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

9.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
9.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'knowledge' — sure, established knowing; awareness of facts based on evidence, the opposite of ignorance or guesswork.
10.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending is the indefinite nominative: the 'n' sound (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('some knowledge', not 'the knowledge'), and the nominative case typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing whose existence is being affirmed.

11.meaning: And I — the standalone first-person singular pronoun 'I,' here joined by 'and.' As a detached pronoun it stands on its own (typically as subject), unlike the attached endings.
11.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and.' 'anā' is the independent (detached) pronoun 'I,' used for emphasis or to begin/identify the subject; it does not take a case ending and is fixed in form.

12.meaning: I call you (plural) — the speaker is summoning, inviting, or calling out to the addressed group, typically toward belief, guidance, or a cause.

parts.en: I call / I invite (first-person singular imperfect)

12.grammar: An imperfect (mudāriʿ) verb, Form I, first-person singular, from the defective (nāqiṣ) root d-ʿ-w — defective because the wāw is the final radical (lām al-fiʿl), not the middle one. The a- prefix marks first person; the stem -dʿū retains the wāw as a long vowel in the imperfect indicative. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object pronoun ('you all'). Together: 'I call/invite you all'. The imperfect tense describes an ongoing or habitual action.
12.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, to invite, to summon, to supplicate

13.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
13.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

14.meaning: One who is mighty, invincible, and unassailable — possessing overwhelming might and dignity that none can overcome; also carries the sense of being precious and held in high honor. As a divine name it points to Allah's irresistible power.
14.grammar: A definite adjective/noun on the intensive paradigm faʿīl, denoting a deeply established quality. The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the Mighty') or follows a preposition.
14.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, invincibility, honor

15.meaning: The Oft-Forgiving — an intensive divine name: Allah who forgives abundantly and repeatedly, covering and pardoning sins in a superlative degree.
15.grammar: Al-Ghaffār is a divine name on the faʿʿāl intensive pattern, indicating habitual or superlative action — far beyond a single act of forgiveness. The definite article al- is required for divine names used in an attributive or vocative context. The kasra ending -i marks the genitive case, typically because the name follows a preposition or is the second term of an iḍāfa ('the Most-Forgiving').
15.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, to cover, to pardon; concealing faults with mercy

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: Part of a fixed expression 'lā jarama' meaning 'no doubt / assuredly / it is inevitable that'. The word 'jarama' here conveys necessity or certainty — that something is bound to be true or earned without escape.

parts.en: fixed final vowel (3rd person masculine singular / built-in ending)

2.grammar: Originally a past-tense verb ('it was earned/made binding'), now used in the frozen expression 'lā jarama' to mean 'no doubt / assuredly / inevitably'. The final '-a' is the third-person masculine singular ending of that old verb form, but in this set phrase the whole functions as an affirmation of certainty rather than an ordinary verb.
2.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to earn, commit, make binding; (root sense) to cut, acquire

3.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that …' or 'only that' — it introduces and emphasizes a fact as the content of a thought or statement; 'anna' asserts ('indeed/that') and the attached 'mā' often gives a restrictive sense ('that … is only …').
3.grammar: A combination of the emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with 'mā'. 'Anna' introduces a noun-clause as the object of verbs like 'think' or 'know', putting the following noun in the accusative. Joined with 'mā' it frequently carries a limiting force, 'only/merely'. Particles like this do not themselves take case endings.
3.root: — (particles; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: You (plural) call me — the addressed group calls or invites the speaker (toward something, often disbelief or false worship); a statement of what they do.

parts.en: me (first-person singular object pronoun — nūn al-wiqāya + yā')

4.grammar: Identical in morphology to id 431 but without the wa- prefix. An imperfect second-person masculine plural verb from the defective root d-ʿ-w; ta- marks second person, -ūna marks masculine plural indicative. The suffix -nī is the full first-person singular object pronoun, consisting of nūn al-wiqāya and the yā' pronoun, both present and unshortened. The indicative -ūna indicates a simple declarative statement about an ongoing or habitual action: 'You (all) call me'.
4.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, to invite, to summon, to supplicate

5.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
5.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

6.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not'. Unlike a simple particle, it behaves like a verb (frozen in the past-tense form) and serves to deny that something is the case, cancelling an assertion of being.
6.grammar: A defective verb fixed in the 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'). The final -a is its frozen ending; it does not conjugate for tense like other verbs. Grammatically it raises its subject to the nominative and puts its predicate in the accusative, functioning to negate a state of being.

7.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
7.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

8.meaning: A call, an invitation, a claim — can mean a call to worship, a supplication addressed to Allah, or a claim/argument put forward; the act or result of calling out.

parts.en: a call / an invitation / a claim (indefinite nominative)

8.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar or instance noun) in the indefinite nominative case, marked by the ḍamma + tanwīn ending -un. The feminine tā' marbūṭa (-a/-at) ending is part of the word's form (daʿwa). The nominative here indicates the word functions as subject or predicate in a sentence. Indefinite signals a general, unspecified instance: 'a call', 'any claim/invitation'.
8.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, to invite, to summon, to supplicate

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

10.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
10.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
10.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

11.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
12.root: — (particle)

13.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
13.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
13.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

14.meaning: 'And that …' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle anna, which introduces and emphasizes a statement, asserting a fact emphatically (roughly 'and indeed that …'), and grammatically governs the noun that follows it.
14.grammar: A conjunction wa ('and') prefixed to anna, an emphatic particle meaning 'that' (asserting a fact). Anna puts the following noun into the accusative case and typically links a clause to a preceding verb of saying, knowing, or perceiving.

15.meaning: Our return, our being brought back — the final return to Allah for judgment; the fact that all will be returned to Him.

parts.en: return / place of return (noun of place/time, accusative or construct state)

15.grammar: Maradda is a noun of place/time (mafʿal pattern from r-d-d), meaning 'the place/act of returning'. In a possessive construction (iḍāfa), the noun loses its tanwīn and the following pronoun -nā functions as the possessing second term. The fatḥa (-a) on the stem here is the construct-state vowel, and the form also carries an accusative sense when governed by a preposition or verb in context. Together: 'our return', 'our being sent back'.
15.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to return, to send back, to bring back

16.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
16.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

17.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
17.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

18.meaning: 'And that …' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle anna, which introduces and emphasizes a statement, asserting a fact emphatically (roughly 'and indeed that …'), and grammatically governs the noun that follows it.
18.grammar: A conjunction wa ('and') prefixed to anna, an emphatic particle meaning 'that' (asserting a fact). Anna puts the following noun into the accusative case and typically links a clause to a preceding verb of saying, knowing, or perceiving.

19.meaning: Those who are wasteful or excessive; people who habitually overstep proper bounds, squander, or transgress moderation.
19.grammar: An active participle ('the ones who do X') with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative or genitive — the form used when such a word is an object or follows a preposition.
19.root: س-ر-ف (s-r-f) — to exceed the limit, waste, be extravagant

20.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
20.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

21.meaning: 'Companions / people of, dwellers, owners' — those closely associated with something, its inseparable folk, fellows, or inmates; literally the people who 'keep company with' a thing.
21.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of ṣāḥib, 'companion'). The '-u' ending is nominative, typically marking the subject of a sentence; it appears here without nunation because the word is in a possessive construction ('companions OF …') with a following noun.

22.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
22.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

1.meaning: And you (plural) will remember / will come to remember — a future recollection, often of a warning that was given and ignored, which will become apparent at a later, unavoidable moment.

parts.en: you (plural) remember / you (all) will recall (second-person masculine plural imperfect)

1.grammar: The fa- is a consequential conjunction ('so', 'then'). The sa- prefix attached to the verb is the marker of the near or definite future in Arabic, equivalent to 'will' in English.
