6.meaning: Creation / the act of creating — the bringing of things into existence, or the created order that results; also denotes how something is fashioned or formed.
6.grammar: A verbal noun ('creating / creation'). The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically links the word to a following noun ('the creation OF …') or follows a preposition.

7.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
7.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
7.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

8.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
8.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.
8.root: — (particle)

9.meaning: More numerous, greater in quantity, the greater part or 'most'. It is the comparative/superlative form built from 'kathīr' (many), expressing 'more' or 'the most' in number or amount.
9.grammar: The pattern af'al makes this an 'elative' (comparative/superlative: 'more/most'). The -a ending is accusative, the case used for the object of a verb or for many adverbial roles.

10.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
10.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
10.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

11.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
11.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

12.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
12.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'
12.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: 'They are equal / it is the same' — to be on a par, level, or alike; to stand even with one another with no difference of value.
2.grammar: A Form VIII present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it is equal'). The 'ya-' prefix marks a present action; the weak final letter (from the root's last 'w/y') appears as the long ending. It expresses things being on the same level.

3.meaning: 'The blind one' — a person lacking sight. Often used figuratively for one who cannot perceive truth or guidance.
3.grammar: A definite descriptive noun/adjective ('the blind') marked by 'al-' ('the'), built on the pattern used for colours and bodily traits. It ends in a fixed long '-ā' vowel and does not change its ending for case — the form stays the same whether subject or object.
3.root: ع-م-ي (ʿ-m-y) — blindness, loss of sight or insight

4.meaning: 'And the seeing one' — a person who possesses sight; figuratively one who perceives clearly and has insight. Built on the intensive 'doer' pattern, it suggests one fully endowed with vision.
4.grammar: A definite noun/adjective joined by 'wa' ('and') and marked by 'al-' ('the'). It follows the 'faʿīl' pattern, which describes someone strongly characterized by a quality (here, seeing). The '-u' ending is the nominative case, the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being identified.

5.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
5.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.
5.root: — (relative pronoun)

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
6.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

7.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
7.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

8.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
8.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
8.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

9.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
9.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

10.meaning: The evildoer, the one who does wrong or harm — a person who perpetrates evil, sin, or injury against others or against what is right.

parts.en: the evildoer / the one who does wrong

10.grammar: Definite active participle in the nominative case. Musīʾ is the Form IV active participle (mufʿil pattern) of the root meaning to do evil or harm. The -u ending before the hamza is the nominative case marker, indicating the word is in subject position. The definite article specifies a known or representative evildoer.

11.meaning: Little, small, scant — small in amount, value, or number; trifling.
11.grammar: An adjective on the stable fa'īl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, used here as it describes a noun that is itself accusative ('a little [thing]').
11.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — to be few, little, scant

12.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
12.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
12.root: — (particle; no root)

13.meaning: 'you (all) take heed / call to mind' — to reflect, remember, and let a reminder sink in so as to be admonished by it.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb of the reflective (Form V) pattern, 'to keep reminding oneself, take heed.' Note the two ta- letters: the first ta- is the present-tense second-person prefix (the person marker, 'you'), while the second ta- belongs to the verb's pattern itself. The plural-and-indicative suffix -ūna (here split as -ū…-na) marks the masculine plural ('you all') in the plain present/future ('you take heed').
13.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: A noun meaning 'the Hour' — most particularly the Last Hour, the appointed time of the world's end and the Resurrection; literally a portion of time, an hour, or a moment.
2.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- (its l assimilates into the following 'sun letter' s, hence the doubled s). The -a ending is the accusative case, the case typically taken by the direct object of a verb or by what follows certain particles.
2.root: س-و-ع (s-w-ʿ) — a span of time, an hour; the appointed Hour

3.meaning: An emphatic 'is surely coming / bound to arrive' — affirming that something is certainly approaching and will inevitably occur. It is the feminine active participle 'coming/arriving', fronted by an emphatic lām.
3.grammar: The lā- prefix is an emphatic particle ('surely'). The word is a feminine active participle ('she who comes'); the -at- is the feminine marker and the final -un combines the -u (nominative) case — used for a subject or predicate — with tanwīn -n marking it indefinite. So: 'is surely coming'.
3.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, approach, bring

4.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
4.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

5.meaning: Doubt, suspicion, disquieting uncertainty — the kind of wavering that unsettles the heart, stronger than a passing question. It names the state of not being at rest about whether something is true.
5.grammar: A masculine singular noun shown with an -a ending and no tanwin. This is the accusative (mansub) noun governed by the negating particle la — its ism — taking a bare form to express absolute negation, conveying that the whole category is ruled out ('there is no doubt whatsoever').
5.root: ر-ي-ب (r-y-b) — doubt, disquiet

6.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
6.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

7.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
7.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.

8.meaning: More numerous, greater in quantity, the greater part or 'most'. It is the comparative/superlative form built from 'kathīr' (many), expressing 'more' or 'the most' in number or amount.
8.grammar: The pattern af'al makes this an 'elative' (comparative/superlative: 'more/most'). The -a ending is accusative, the case used for the object of a verb or for many adverbial roles.
8.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much/many, abundance

9.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
9.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
9.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

10.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
10.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

11.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
11.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: Your Lord — your Master, Owner, and Sustainer; rabb denotes the One who creates, possesses, nurtures, and governs, joined here to 'you' (plural).
2.grammar: The noun rabb means Lord/Master/Nurturer. The -u before the suffix is the nominative, the case of a subject or of the word identified as 'the one who…'. The attached -kum ('your,' plural) is lengthened to -kumu to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with 'the.'
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, own, master; to sustain and bring to perfection

3.meaning: Call upon Me, supplicate Me, invoke Me — a divine command to direct all prayer, petition, and worship toward Allah alone.
3.grammar: Form I imperative, second-person masculine plural + first-person singular object pronoun. The imperative id'ʿū is the plural command form with the wāw plural marker (-ū). The attached pronoun -nī ('me') is the direct object, specifying that the supplication is to be directed to the speaker (Allah). Together: 'all of you, call upon Me'.
3.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — calling, inviting, supplicating

4.meaning: I will respond, I will answer — the promise of a direct divine response to those who call; to answer a prayer or petition.

parts.en: I will respond / I will answer

4.grammar: Form X imperfect (or jussive), first-person singular. The a- prefix marks first-person singular. Form X (istajaaba) carries the sense of responding or answering back. The final sukūn (absence of short vowel, written as jussive) is used in apodoses of conditional-style promises and response clauses — here signalling the assured consequence: 'I will answer (you)'.

5.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

6.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
6.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'they act arrogantly, deem themselves great, behave with haughty pride' — to puff oneself up and disdain to submit or yield.
8.grammar: A present-tense (form X) verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The full -ūna ending signals the indicative mood, used for a plain, ongoing statement of fact. Form X here carries the sense of considering oneself great.
8.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, bigness; here, self-magnification and pride

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

9.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

10.meaning: My worship, worship of me, my devotion — the act of servitude, submission, and dedicated devotion directed toward Allah, here expressed as belonging to or owed to the speaker (Allah).
10.grammar: Feminine verbal noun in the genitive/construct state + first-person singular possessive pronoun. ʿIbādah is the verbal noun of Form I denoting the act of worship and total servitude. The -ti ending is the feminine marker in the construct state (iḍāfa), with the final tāʾ marbūṭa changing to -t- before a suffix. The pronoun -ī ('my') makes it 'My worship' — worship belonging to or directed at Allah.
10.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — worship, servitude, being a servant

11.meaning: They will enter — the verb conveys a future entry into a place, used for both dignified and humiliating entries depending on context.
11.grammar: Active indicative, Form I, third-person masculine plural, future tense. The sa- prefix signals a definite future. The -ūna ending marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural) and, in the indicative mood, signals a statement of fact rather than a command or wish.

12.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
12.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
12.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

13.meaning: In a state of utter humiliation and subjugation — abased, brought low, despised.

parts.en: stem: one who is debased/humiliated (active participle)

13.grammar: Active participle (Form I), masculine sound plural, in the accusative/genitive case. The -īna ending (oblique plural) marks the word as an adverbial complement or object — describing the manner or state of the subject. It functions like an adjective or circumstantial phrase ('while being humiliated').
13.root: د-خ-ر (d-kh-r) — to be abased, humbled, brought low

1.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
1.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: 'He made,' 'He appointed,' 'He set up' — to bring about, fashion, or assign something to a state or role. Beyond mere 'making,' it often means rendering one thing into another or establishing something for a purpose.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer and places the action in the completed past ('he made / appointed'). This verb commonly governs two objects, in the sense of 'made X into Y.'
3.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint

4.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something is done or given.
4.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). Such prepositions assign a benefit, purpose, or recipient. The pronoun's vowel appears as '-u' (kumu) to ease pronunciation when a word follows.

5.meaning: The night — al-layl is the period of darkness from sunset to dawn; the dark portion of the day-night cycle, a time of covering, rest and stillness.
5.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative case, the ending typically given to the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or used adverbially for time ('the night').
5.root: ل-ي-ل (l-y-l) — night, darkness

6.meaning: So that you may find rest and stillness — to settle down, grow calm, and dwell at ease, the restlessness quieted into repose and tranquil dwelling.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb preceded by li- ('so that, in order to'), which expresses purpose and puts the verb in the subjunctive. The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the -ū ending marks masculine plural ('you all') — note the subjunctive after li- drops the final -na.
6.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to be still, to rest, to dwell

7.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
7.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

8.meaning: And the daytime — the period of daylight between dawn and sunset, the bright span of the day as opposed to night.
8.grammar: A masculine noun with the prefix wa- ('and') and the definite article (here assimilated as n-nahār). The final -a ending is the accusative case, which commonly marks the object of a verb or the thing being pointed to.
8.root: ن-ه-ر (n-h-r) — daytime, daylight; (also) to flow

9.meaning: Giving light to see by — making things visible, illuminating so that sight is possible. The active participle describes something that grants visibility or causes one to see clearly.
9.grammar: An active participle of form IV (the mu- prefix marks 'the one doing/causing the action'). The -an ending marks the accusative with indefiniteness, commonly used for a descriptive state ('as something giving light'), and the final -n (nunation) signals 'a/some'.
9.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — to see, to perceive, sight

10.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
10.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

12.meaning: An emphatic statement that someone is truly the holder or owner of something. The opening lām is a particle of emphasis ('surely/indeed'), and dhū means 'owner of, possessor of, the one endowed with' — it is a word that always governs a following noun to say someone is rich in or characterized by that thing.
12.grammar: The la- prefix is the 'lām of emphasis' that strengthens a statement ('indeed, surely'). Dhū is one of the special 'five nouns'; its long -ū ending marks the nominative (subject) case, the form used when this word is the doer or the thing being described, and it must be followed by a noun in the genitive ('possessor OF …').

13.meaning: Bounty, grace, favor; an overflowing generosity or surplus given freely. It denotes goodness and abundance bestowed beyond what is owed or expected, and by extension excellence or superiority.
13.grammar: The -in ending is genitive plus 'tanwīn' (the -n indicating indefiniteness, 'a bounty'). The genitive case typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF bounty') or follows a preposition.
13.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — bounty, grace, excess goodness, superiority

14.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
14.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
14.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

15.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
15.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
15.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

16.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
16.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.

17.meaning: More numerous, greater in quantity, the greater part or 'most'. It is the comparative/superlative form built from 'kathīr' (many), expressing 'more' or 'the most' in number or amount.
17.grammar: The pattern af'al makes this an 'elative' (comparative/superlative: 'more/most'). The -a ending is accusative, the case used for the object of a verb or for many adverbial roles.

18.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
18.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
18.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

19.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
19.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

20.meaning: They give thanks, they are grateful — to acknowledge a kindness and respond to it with gratitude and praise. The verb conveys recognizing a benefit and honoring its giver.
20.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks third-person masculine plural ('they …'). The full -ūna ending shows the indicative mood, the plain factual form used for ongoing or habitual action ('they do thank').

1.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' — a pointing word that singles out something distant or already mentioned, addressed to a group of people ('that, O you [plural]').
1.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', built from the base 'dhā' plus the distance-marker 'l-' and the plural-addressee particle '-kum' ('you all'). The final 'u' on '-kumu' is a connecting vowel used when the next word begins with a definite article. It does not change for case.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: Your (plural) Lord — 'Rabb' means the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and brings a thing to its completion. It combines lordship with loving upbringing and care.
3.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The suffix '-kum' means 'your' (plural possessor). The '-u' on 'rabbu' before the suffix is the nominative case, marking the word as a subject or as a predicate standing on its own.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain, own

4.meaning: Creator, Originator, Maker — the one who brings things into existence and gives them their form. As a title of Allah it denotes the sole Author of all that exists.
4.grammar: An active participle ('one who creates') used as a noun. The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or a noun standing on its own. Often heads a possessive phrase ('Creator OF …').

5.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
5.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.
5.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, comprising the whole

6.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
6.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
6.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

7.meaning: No / there is no — a negating particle. In the pattern 'lā + noun,' it gives absolute, categorical negation: 'there is no … at all.'
7.grammar: A particle of negation. Used for total denial of a class of things ('no … whatsoever'); when it governs a following indefinite noun it negates that thing absolutely. It is an indeclinable particle with no case ending of its own.

8.meaning: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
8.grammar: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
8.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
10.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

11.meaning: An interrogative of manner or place meaning 'how?', 'in what way?', or 'whence / from where?'. It expresses wonder or challenge at how something could be so, often implying 'how on earth…?'.
11.grammar: A connective 'fa' ('so/then') joined to an indeclinable question-word. Being a fixed particle, it has no case ending; it opens a question about manner or source and carries a tone of astonishment or rebuke.

12.meaning: To be turned away, diverted, or deluded — driven from truth to falsehood, made to deviate from what is right. The passive sense is 'to be deflected / led astray' from a correct course.
12.grammar: A present/future-tense passive verb, second-person masculine plural: 'you (all) are turned away'. The vowel pattern (u-a) marks it passive — the subject has the action done to it — and the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject in the ongoing (indicative) mood.
12.root: أ-ف-ك (ʾ-f-k) — turning away, deceiving, falsehood

1.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
1.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
1.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

2.meaning: He is turned away, averted, led astray — used of someone who is diverted from truth or sound reason.
2.grammar: Passive imperfect (Form I), third-person masculine singular. The u- prefix vowel on the first syllable signals a passive voice. The -u ending is the indicative ending, marking a statement of fact (present or habitual).
2.root: أ-ف-ك (ʾ-f-k) — to turn away, invert, pervert, lead astray

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
4.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

5.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
5.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
5.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'they knowingly reject / deny / repudiate.' Its distinctive sense is denying something one inwardly recognizes to be true — rejection against better knowledge.

parts.en: they (the prefix marking a third-person subject)
plural marker, with the -na of the ongoing/present

7.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks 'they,' and -ūna marks a plural subject and an ongoing or repeated action. The retained -na is the mark of the indicative mood, the verb's default unbroken form.
7.root: ج-ح-د (j-ḥ-d) — to deny or reject what one knows to be true

1.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
1.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: 'He made,' 'He appointed,' 'He set up' — to bring about, fashion, or assign something to a state or role. Beyond mere 'making,' it often means rendering one thing into another or establishing something for a purpose.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer and places the action in the completed past ('he made / appointed'). This verb commonly governs two objects, in the sense of 'made X into Y.'
3.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint

4.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something is done or given.
4.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). Such prepositions assign a benefit, purpose, or recipient. The pronoun's vowel appears as '-u' (kumu) to ease pronunciation when a word follows.

5.meaning: 'the earth,' 'the ground,' 'the land' — the earth as a whole, or the land/ground beneath us. It denotes the terrestrial expanse on which creatures live and walk.
5.grammar: A definite noun ('the earth'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative (the 'object' case) — the role of the thing acted upon, e.g. the direct object of a verb. The prefixed 'al-' makes it definite, 'the earth.'
5.root: أ-ر-ض (ʼ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

6.meaning: A resting-place, a firm abode, a place of settlement and stability — somewhere one settles and remains.

parts.en: noun: a place/state of settlement, stability

6.grammar: Noun of place and state (ism makān/ism hayʾah) on the faʿāl pattern, masculine singular indefinite, accusative case. The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥ) marks an indefinite word in the accusative — it typically follows a verb as its object or complement, or follows a preposition's logical structure.
6.root: ق-ر-ر (q-r-r) — to settle, be established, remain fixed

7.meaning: 'and the sky,' 'and the heaven' — the sky or heaven above, the visible expanse overhead, joined by 'and.' 'Samāʼ' covers everything that rises above and canopies the earth.
7.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') prefixed to the definite noun 'the sky.' The '-a' ending marks the accusative (the 'object' case), the role of the thing acted upon. 'Al-' makes it definite ('the sky'); the 's' is doubled because it is a 'sun letter' that absorbs the 'l' of 'al-' in pronunciation.
7.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness, what is above (sky/heaven)

8.meaning: 'a building,' 'a structure,' 'an edifice raised up' — something constructed and built up, hence a canopy or roof-like structure. The word names the act or product of building, an erected, well-formed construction.
8.grammar: An indefinite verbal noun ('a building, edifice'). The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks the accusative case with indefiniteness — typically the second object of a 'make X into Y' verb or a complement describing what something is rendered as ('as a structure').
8.root: ب-ن-ي (b-n-y) — to build, construct, raise up

9.meaning: And He shaped you, gave you your form — the verb conveys active fashioning of the body's outward shape and appearance.

parts.en: he shaped/formed (Form II verb, past tense)

9.grammar: Form II (faʿʿala) perfect tense, third-person masculine singular, with an attached second-person masculine plural object pronoun. The Form II doubling of the middle radical intensifies the action — thorough, purposeful shaping. The -a ending on the verb marks a completed past action. The suffix -kum means 'you all' as the direct object.
9.root: ص-و-ر (ṣ-w-r) — to shape, depict, give form

10.meaning: And He made it excellent, did it perfectly — performing an action in the most beautiful and complete manner possible.

parts.en: he did excellently/perfected (Form IV verb, past tense)

10.grammar: Form IV (afʿala) perfect tense, third-person masculine singular. The fa- conjunction signals a result following from what preceded. The -a ending marks a completed past action. Form IV here gives a causative-resultative sense: 'he caused it to be excellent / made it beautiful.'

11.meaning: Your forms, your shapes — the outward physical appearances and bodily configurations that have been given to you.
11.grammar: Broken plural of ṣūrah, masculine, with an attached second-person masculine plural possessive pronoun -kum. The noun is in the accusative case (ṣuwara with fatḥa ending), functioning as a direct object. The -kum suffix links it to 'you all' as possessors.
11.root: ص-و-ر (ṣ-w-r) — to shape, depict, give form

12.meaning: And He provided for you, granted you sustenance — to bestow the provision (food, livelihood, and every good) that a creature needs and lives on.
12.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('He provided'). The opening wa- means 'and.' The final -kum is the attached object pronoun 'you (plural).' The -a- vowels are the standard pattern of a plain past-tense verb.
12.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — provision, sustenance, livelihood granted by Allah

13.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
13.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

14.meaning: 'The good/wholesome things' — that which is pure, pleasant, and lawful, especially good and agreeable food.
14.grammar: A descriptive noun ('good, wholesome') made definite by al- ('the') and put in the feminine sound plural. The -āti ending is the feminine plural in the object or genitive state (its counterpart -ātu is the subject form). It names things characterized as pure and good.
14.root: ط-ي-ب (ṭ-y-b) — to be good, pure, wholesome, pleasant

15.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' — a pointing word that singles out something distant or already mentioned, addressed to a group of people ('that, O you [plural]').
15.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', built from the base 'dhā' plus the distance-marker 'l-' and the plural-addressee particle '-kum' ('you all'). The final 'u' on '-kumu' is a connecting vowel used when the next word begins with a definite article. It does not change for case.
15.root: — (demonstrative pronoun; no triliteral root)

16.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
16.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

17.meaning: Your (plural) Lord — 'Rabb' means the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and brings a thing to its completion. It combines lordship with loving upbringing and care.
17.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The suffix '-kum' means 'your' (plural possessor). The '-u' on 'rabbu' before the suffix is the nominative case, marking the word as a subject or as a predicate standing on its own.
17.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain, own

18.meaning: So blessed is — an expression of exalted, transcendent blessing and majesty, far beyond what any creature can possess. It is used exclusively of Allah and conveys the idea that He is the ultimate source of all goodness and abundance.

parts.en: is/was supremely blessed, exalted in blessing (Form VI)

18.grammar: Form VI (tafāʿala) perfect tense, third-person masculine singular. This form of the root is used exclusively in the Qur'an as a divine attribute — never for creation. The -a ending is the perfect-tense marker for third-person masculine singular, indicating a completed or established state.

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
19.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

20.meaning: The Lord of — owner, master and sustainer who creates, possesses and governs. Of Allah it names the One who brings up and maintains all that exists.
20.grammar: The noun 'rabb' with the final -u marking the nominative case (subject or predicate: '… is the Lord'). Standing before a following noun it carries the sense 'Lord of …'. It combines ownership, authority and nurturing care.

21.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
21.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
21.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
1.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

2.meaning: 'the Ever-Living / the Living One' — possessing life in the fullest, absolute, and eternal sense: life that never began and never ends, the source of all life. As a divine name it affirms perfect, undying life.
2.grammar: A definite adjective/noun ('the Living'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun in apposition (a descriptive title) to such a subject.

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
4.grammar: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
4.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

5.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
5.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
5.root: — (particle)

6.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
6.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

7.meaning: So call upon Him / invoke Him — a command to call on, supplicate, or appeal to 'Him,' joined with 'so/then.'
7.grammar: A command addressed to a group of males: 'call upon Him!' The fa- prefix means 'so/then.' The -ū ending marks a plural 'you' commanded to act, and the attached -hu means 'Him.'
7.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, supplicate

8.meaning: Being sincere and single-hearted — making one's devotion purely and exclusively for Allah, with no rival motive mixed in. It describes a group of people in this state.

parts.en: one who is sincere / devotes purely

8.grammar: A Form IV active participle (pattern muf'il, from the verb akhlaṣa 'to make pure / devote sincerely'), describing the one who purifies and dedicates his devotion. It is in the sound masculine plural, and the '-īna' ending marks the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) case, so it describes a plural group as those who make their worship purely and sincerely for Allah.
8.root: خ-ل-ص (kh-l-ṣ) — to be pure, sincere, unmixed

9.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
9.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

10.meaning: The dīn — a deep term covering religion, the way of life, the path of obedience and worship owed to Allah, and the reckoning/recompense for it; a complete system of belief and practice with accountability.
10.grammar: A definite noun ('al-' = 'the') with the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the object of certain particles.

11.meaning: All praise, commendation, and grateful acknowledgement — the recognition that beauty, goodness, and perfection rightly belong to and are owed to the one being praised. As a definite noun with the article 'al-', it conveys that the totality of praise is encompassed.
11.grammar: A definite noun (carrying the article 'al-', 'the'). The final '-u' ending is nominative: it marks the word as the subject or main topic of a statement — the thing being talked about or the doer of an action, rather than its object.
11.root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d) — to praise, to commend, to give thanks

12.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
12.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

13.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
13.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
13.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

14.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
14.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
14.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
2.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

3.meaning: 'I was forbidden / prohibited' — to be barred or restrained from doing something, told not to do it.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice (the inner vowels nuhī- mark 'was-done-to' rather than 'did'). The suffix -tu marks a first-person singular subject ('I'), so the form means 'I was forbidden'. The doer of the forbidding is left unstated.
3.root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y) — forbidding, prohibiting, restraining

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: 'That I worship / serve' — to worship, to serve in humble devotion and obedience as a servant before his Master.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, taken when the verb is governed by a preceding particle (such as 'that/to'), giving the sense 'that I worship' or 'to worship'.
5.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — worship, service, humble devotion

6.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
6.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) call upon, invoke, summon, or pray to.' The root spans calling out, naming, inviting, and supplicating — especially calling on someone for help.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the doers. The final -na is the indicative marker, signalling an ongoing or habitual action (a complete, non-shortened present-tense verb).
7.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, invoke, summon, pray

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
8.root: — (preposition)

9.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
9.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
9.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the point that' something occurred — pointing to the moment a past event took place and often implying that one thing happened upon the completion of another. In other uses it can carry the sense of 'not yet'.
11.grammar: A particle (a small connecting word), not a noun or verb, so it has no case or tense ending. It introduces a clause and links it in time to another event — most often 'when / as soon as' a past action happened.

12.meaning: They have come to me, they came to me — the arrival of something or someone at the speaker.

parts.en: came/have come (past tense verb, third-person masculine singular)
to me (first-person singular indirect object pronoun, with nūn wikāyah)
me (first-person singular attached pronoun completing the junction)

12.grammar: Form I perfect tense, third-person masculine singular (the -a ending is the morphological marker of 3ms). In Arabic, a verb preceding its plural subject may appear in the singular by standard agreement rules, so jāa here is morphologically singular even though the subject it precedes is plural. The -ni element is a nūn wikāyah (protective nūn) inserted before the first-person pronoun -ya to preserve the kasra vowel of the preceding syllable. Together -niya means 'to me' as indirect object.
12.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, to arrive

13.meaning: The clear proofs / evident signs — plainly manifest, self-evident pieces of evidence that make the truth unmistakable.

parts.en: clear proofs / evident signs (the final -u is the nominative case ending, marking the subject)

13.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun (with 'al-' = 'the') meaning 'clear proofs.' The plural ending 'āt' marks a feminine plural, and the final -u is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the noun as the subject/doer of a sentence ('… the clear proofs came to you'). The pattern 'bayyina' denotes something that makes things plainly evident.
13.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — clarity, distinctness; to make plain or evident

14.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
14.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
14.root: — (preposition)

15.meaning: 'My Lord' — the word 'rabb' denotes the Lord, Master, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, owns, governs and brings a thing to its full development; with the attached 'my' it expresses one's own Lord and Caretaker.
15.grammar: A noun followed by the possessive ending '-ī' meaning 'my', which joins to the noun and also serves the genitive (possessive) relationship. The attached '-ī' both makes the noun definite and shows ownership: 'my Lord'.
15.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, sustaining

16.meaning: And I have been commanded — a past-tense statement in which the speaker reports being ordered or instructed by another; the doer of the commanding is left unnamed, so the focus rests on the speaker as the one under orders.
16.grammar: A past-tense passive verb with the prefixed 'wa' ('and'). The inner vowel pattern 'u-i' shows it is passive ('was commanded', no named commander), and the '-tu' ending makes the speaker its subject ('I was commanded').
16.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — commanding, ordering; an affair or matter

17.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
17.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

18.meaning: To submit, to surrender entirely — handing oneself over in complete willing obedience and devotion.

parts.en: I was commanded to submit / it was ordained that I submit (Form IV passive perfect)

18.grammar: Form IV (afʿala) passive perfect, third-person masculine singular, on the ufʿila pattern. The u- prefix vowel and the -i- vowel on the second syllable are the unmistakable markers of the passive perfect in Arabic. The -a ending marks the third-person masculine singular. In context it functions as an injunctive passive of command: 'it has been ordained / I am commanded to submit,' expressing a divine directive reported by the speaker.

19.meaning: 'To/for the Lord' — the preposition 'to/for' joined to rabb, a richly loaded term meaning the Lord, Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, sustains, and brings to maturity all He governs.
19.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition ('to/for') that places the following noun in the genitive. Accordingly rabb takes the -i (genitive) ending, marking it as governed by the preposition and typically standing in construct with a following noun ('Lord OF …').

20.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
20.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
20.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
1.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: 'He created you' — He brought you into existence, originating and shaping you. The verb denotes bringing something into being and giving it its form and proportion, here with 'you (plural)' as the one(s) created.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb with an attached object pronoun. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer in the completed past ('he created'). The suffix '-kum' is the object 'you (plural),' i.e. the ones to whom the action was done.
3.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, originate, shape

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: 'Dust / earth / soil.' The noun turāb denotes dust or dry earth — the fine soil of the ground.
5.grammar: A masculine noun. The -in ending marks it as indefinite ('dust / some dust') and in the genitive case — the form used after a preposition (e.g., 'from …') or when linked to a preceding noun.
5.root: ت-ر-ب (t-r-b) — dust, earth, soil

6.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
6.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

8.meaning: A drop of fluid; a tiny quantity of sperm/seminal fluid — by extension the minute beginning from which a human is formed.
8.grammar: A feminine noun (the '-a(t)' is its feminine form). The final '-in' (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a …') and in the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
8.root: ن-ط-ف (n-ṭ-f) — to drip, trickle; a drop of fluid

9.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
9.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: A clinging, suspended substance — in embryological usage, the clot or leech-like mass that clings to the uterine wall in early development.

parts.en: a clinging thing, a clot (indefinite genitive noun)

11.grammar: Feminine singular noun, indefinite, genitive case. The -in ending (tanwīn kasr) marks indefiniteness and the genitive case — it typically follows a preposition or appears in a possessive chain. The kasra tanwīn signals 'of a/an …' relationship.

12.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
12.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

13.meaning: He brings you out, He extracts you — the act of causing someone to come forth from one state or place into another.
13.grammar: Form IV (afʿala) imperfect active, third-person masculine singular, with an attached second-person masculine plural object pronoun -kum. The -u ending marks indicative mood — a straightforward statement of fact (present or habitual action).
13.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, emerge; causative: to bring out

14.meaning: A child, an infant — a young human being in the early stage of life, before strength or maturity.

parts.en: a child, an infant (indefinite accusative noun)

14.grammar: Masculine singular noun, indefinite, accusative case. The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥ) marks indefiniteness and the accusative — functioning here as a circumstantial complement ('as a child', 'in the state of being a child').
14.root: ط-ف-ل (ṭ-f-l) — childhood, a young child

15.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
15.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

16.meaning: In order that you may reach — expressing purpose: so that the subject attains a particular stage or destination.

parts.en: in order to / so that (lām of purpose)
you reach/attain (imperfect subjunctive, second-person masculine plural)

16.grammar: The lām li- is the particle of purpose, which triggers the subjunctive mood. The verb is Form I imperfect, second-person masculine plural, subjunctive — hence the -ū ending (the nūn of the indicative is dropped in the subjunctive). Together they mean 'so that you all may reach.'
16.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, attain, arrive at

17.meaning: Your full strength, your prime — the peak of physical and mental vigour that a human being reaches in early adulthood.

parts.en: full strength, prime of life (noun, accusative)

17.grammar: The noun ashudd is a plural of intensity (or a singular of unique form), in the accusative case as the object of the verb 'reach'. The attached pronoun -kum makes it possessive: 'your full strength.' The word has no standard singular and is used in this fixed form.

18.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
18.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

19.meaning: In order that you may be — expressing purpose: so that the subject comes to exist in a certain state.

parts.en: in order to / so that (lām of purpose)
you become/are (imperfect subjunctive, second-person masculine plural)

19.grammar: The lām li- triggers the subjunctive, dropping the nūn of the indicative plural. The verb is Form I imperfect (kāna 'to be'), second-person masculine plural, subjunctive — 'so that you all may be/become.' Used to express purpose or result.
19.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

20.meaning: Old men, elders — persons who have reached advanced age, with its attendant weakness and white hair.

parts.en: old men, elders (broken plural, indefinite accusative)

20.grammar: Broken plural of shaykh, masculine, indefinite, accusative case. The -an (tanwīn fatḥ) ending marks indefiniteness and accusative — functioning as a predicate or object complement describing the state the subject reaches.

21.meaning: A combination meaning 'and from / among / of you (plural)'. It conveys partitive or source sense — 'some of you' or 'from your side'.
21.grammar: A particle phrase: the conjunction wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, among, of'), with the attached pronoun -kum ('you all') as its object. min often expresses origin, separation, or a part of a whole.

22.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
22.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

23.meaning: Is caused to die, is fully taken back — the verb conveys that the soul is received and taken in full by Allah at the moment of death.

parts.en: stem (passive): be taken in full, die (Form V passive)
passive imperfect ending (third-person masculine singular with alif maqṣūra)

23.grammar: Form V (tafaʿʿala) passive imperfect, third-person masculine singular. The -ā ending (written as alif maqṣūra ى) is the passive indicative ending for a verb whose final root letter is wāw or yāʾ. It signals a present/habitual passive action: 'he is/gets taken back/caused to die.'
23.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — to fulfil, to take in full; passive: to die

24.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
24.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

25.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
